clusters.title: Truth value of quantified statements over integers/reals
clusters.technique: For each statement find a witness (for exists) or a counterexample (for forall) in the given universe. Quick tests: n=0, n=1, n=-1, n^2 vs n for 0<n<1 (not integers), and remember n+m=4 with n-m=1 needs n=2.5 (no integer solution).
clusters.what_changes: The list of 4-5 statements A-E (n^2<m, n<m^2, nm=m, n^2+m^2=5 or 6, n+m=4 & n-m=1) and the universe (integers vs reals); the same statements reappear shuffled.
clusters.skip_note: Dec 2023 q42 and June 2024 q22 share almost identical statements; master the n^2/m pattern table and the rest follow.

clusters.title: Match propositional equivalences (implication, biconditional, negation, De Morgan)
clusters.technique: Convert everything to the standard forms: p->q = ~p v q, p<->q = (p^q) v (~p^~q), ~(p->q)= p^~q, ~(p v q)=~p^~q, ~(p<->q)= ~p<->q. Match by elimination using one or two unambiguous pairs.
clusters.what_changes: Which 4 equivalences are listed and the arrangement of the match options.
clusters.skip_note: Same fixed set of identities each time; the rep covers every pair seen.

clusters.title: Converse, inverse, contrapositive, implication terminology match
clusters.technique: p->q: converse q->p, inverse ~p->~q, contrapositive ~q->~p (equivalent to original). Equivalence is p<->q.
clusters.what_changes: Sentences instead of symbols, or symbol forms; order of list items.
clusters.skip_note: Only four terms exist; the rep drills the word-form of the same mapping.

clusters.title: Which pairs are (not) logically equivalent / identify valid equivalence statements
clusters.technique: Use contrapositive, De Morgan, distribution of implication: (p->r)^(q->r) = (p v q)->r while (p^q)->r = (p->r) v (q->r). Test suspicious options with a 2-3 row truth table.
clusters.what_changes: Particular formulas; the trap is distributing implication over wrong connective; 'NOT equivalent' vs 'equivalent' stem.
clusters.skip_note: Same traps (wrong distribution, converse vs contrapositive) recur; nov2020_q3 + nov2021_q21 cover them.

clusters.title: Identify tautologies among given formulas
clusters.technique: Assume the formula is false and try to force a contradiction (false conclusion, true premise); or check the single falsifying assignment for each.
clusters.what_changes: Formulas in 3 variables, 4-5 per question, multi-select options.
clusters.skip_note: Both use the make-it-false method; one rep suffices.

clusters.title: Translate English sentences to propositional logic
clusters.technique: Map: 'neither P nor Q' = ~P ^ ~Q; 'if P then Q' = P->Q; 'necessary for P is Q' = P->Q (P implies Q); 'sufficient' = antecedent; 'only if' = consequent.
clusters.what_changes: Sentences and the P/Q meanings; necessary/sufficient/neither phrasing.
clusters.skip_note: Same phrase-to-connective table; rep includes necessary/sufficient wording.

clusters.title: Quantifier translation (English <-> predicate logic)
clusters.technique: 'Some A are not B' = exists x (A ^ ~B); 'all A are B' = forall x (A -> B); 'X is loved by everyone' = forall x L(x,X). For forall x exists y (x<y): for every x there is a larger y.
clusters.what_changes: Direction of translation (to symbols or to English) and predicate names.
clusters.skip_note: Argument order and exists-with-AND / forall-with-implies are the only traps; one rep is enough.

clusters.title: Negation of quantified statements
clusters.technique: ~exists x Q = forall x ~Q; ~forall x Q = exists x ~Q. 'Some students like hockey' negates to 'every student dislikes hockey'.
clusters.skip_note: Single rule, asked twice with different wording.

clusters.title: Check reflexive/symmetric/antisymmetric/transitive properties of a given relation
clusters.technique: Test reflexive (all (a,a) present), symmetric (every (a,b) has (b,a)), antisymmetric (no a!=b both ways), transitive (check chains). Eliminate options with one failing property. For infinite relations find a counterexample.
clusters.what_changes: The relation (pair list, formula like xv=yu, x<u & y>v, |x-y|<eps, brother-of) and which properties are asked.
clusters.skip_note: All use the same four definitions; do dec2023_q43 + dec2022_q43 and watch for |x-y|<eps (not transitive) and brother-of (not symmetric).

clusters.title: Identify/prove an equivalence relation
clusters.technique: Check reflexive, symmetric, transitive. Equal-mod-k or 'same value of a function' type relations are equivalences; 'f(0)=g(0) or f(1)=g(1)' fails transitivity.
clusters.what_changes: Domain (finite set, functions Z->Z, N x N) and the defining rule.
clusters.skip_note: Same three-property test; the rep is the hardest algebraic version.

clusters.title: Inclusion-exclusion counting with 2 or 3 sets
clusters.technique: |AuB|=|A|+|B|-|AnB|; |AuBuC|=sum singles - sum pairs + triple. Neither = total - union.

clusters.title: Empty-set and nested-set membership/subset
clusters.technique: Distinguish phi (no elements) from {phi} (one element). x in S needs x listed as an element; x subset S needs all elements of x in S.
clusters.what_changes: Which of A-E statements are asked or the match items.

clusters.title: Set algebra identity / operation matching
clusters.technique: A-B = A n B^c; symmetric difference = (A-B)u(B-A); A-(BuC)=(A-B)n(A-C); A-(BnC)=(A-B)u(A-C); A n (B-C)=(AnB)-(AnC). Verify with a Venn or small example.
clusters.skip_note: Same identity table; the rep has all of them.

clusters.title: Poset GLB/LUB and greatest/least element under divisibility
clusters.technique: In (Z+, |): GLB = gcd, LUB = lcm of the set. Greatest element exists only if one element is divisible by all others (and least if one divides all).
clusters.what_changes: The sets and whether asked for bounds or greatest/least elements.
clusters.skip_note: Both reduce to gcd/lcm and divisibility check.

clusters.title: Boolean algebra statement-check (atoms, complement, direct product, NAND/NOR)
clusters.technique: A finite Boolean algebra has 2^n elements (no 5-element one); complements are unique; direct product of Boolean algebras is a Boolean algebra; any network can be built from NAND or NOR alone; two Boolean algebras with the same number of atoms are isomorphic.
clusters.skip_note: Same fact bank; learn the facts once.

clusters.title: Boolean laws and dual expressions matching
clusters.technique: Dual: swap + with ., 0 with 1 (leave literals). Laws: absorption a+ab=a, bound a+1=1, identity a+0=a, distributive.
clusters.skip_note: Pure recall of the law names and dual rule.

clusters.title: Pigeonhole principle (minimum number to guarantee)
clusters.technique: Worst case: fill every box to r-1, then add one: N = k(r-1)+1. For 'at least three hearts' count all non-hearts (39) + 2 hearts, plus 1 = 42.
clusters.skip_note: Same worst-case-plus-one formula; the card version is the only twist.

clusters.title: Stars and bars: integral solutions / balls into bins
clusters.technique: Non-negative solutions of x1+..+xk = n: C(n+k-1, k-1). With lower bounds subtract them from n first (29-1-2-3=23, C(26,3)=2600).
clusters.what_changes: n, k, lower bounds, or balls in distinguishable bins.

clusters.title: Onto functions / distributing distinct objects with every box non-empty
clusters.technique: Onto count = sum_{i=0}^{k} (-1)^i C(k,i)(k-i)^n (= k! S(n,k)). 5 jobs on 4 people = 240; 7 people on 3 floors = 3^7-3*2^7+3 = 1806.
clusters.what_changes: Numbers n and k and the story.

clusters.title: Inclusion-exclusion in counting (bit strings, integers up to N)
clusters.technique: |A u B| = |A|+|B|-|A n B|. Bit strings starting with 1 (2^9), ending 00 (2^8), both (2^7): 640. Odd or perfect square up to 100: 50 odd + 5 even squares (4,16,36,64,100) = 55.

clusters.title: Recurrence relations: set up and solve
clusters.technique: Linear homogeneous: characteristic equation; repeated root r gives (a+bn)r^n (r^2-8r+16 => 4^n and n4^n). Divide and conquer f(n)=a f(n/2)+c: unroll with n=2^K. Stairs: f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2), Fibonacci.
clusters.skip_note: Three recurrence types; do all three once because they differ in method.

clusters.title: Multiplication rule counting (labels, ordered selections)
clusters.technique: Product rule; ordered selection without replacement is nPr: 42*41*40 = 68880. Labels: 26 letters x 99 positive two-digit numbers = 2574.

clusters.title: Handshaking lemma
clusters.technique: Sum of degrees = 2|E|; number of odd-degree vertices is even.
clusters.what_changes: Asked as statements or as 'sum of degrees equals?'

clusters.title: Planarity of drawn graphs
clusters.technique: Look for a K5 or K3,3 subdivision (Kuratowski); otherwise redraw without crossings. Check E<=3V-6 as a quick necessary test.
clusters.what_changes: The figures; format is identical image-based.
clusters.skip_note: Figure-based; solve dec2024 to learn the method.

clusters.title: Graph colouring and bipartite equivalence
clusters.technique: Bipartite = 2-colourable = no odd cycles; trees are 2-colourable; max degree d needs at most d+1 colours; planar graphs are 4-colourable.
clusters.what_changes: Which statements are listed as correct/incorrect.

clusters.title: Hamiltonian sufficient conditions (Dirac/Ore)
clusters.technique: Dirac: n>=3 and deg(v)>=n/2 for all v => Hamiltonian. Ore: deg(v)+deg(w)>=n for each non-adjacent pair. Ore's condition is the sum, not the n/3 trap.

clusters.title: Number of spanning trees of small graphs
clusters.technique: Cayley: K_n has n^(n-2); cycle C_n has n; K2,2=C4 has 4; otherwise Kirchhoff or deletion-contraction (tau(G)=tau(G-e)+tau(G/e)).

clusters.title: Trees and forests: vertex/edge counts
clusters.technique: Tree: E=V-1. Forest with k components: E=V-k, so minimum edges of a graph with k components is n-k. Use sum of degrees = 2E to find unknown n.
clusters.what_changes: Degree sequence or number of vertices/edges.

clusters.title: Standard graph family properties (edges, regularity)
clusters.technique: K_n: n(n-1)/2 edges; C_n: n; W_n (n vertices): 2(n-1), regular only for W4=K4; K_{n,n}: n^2; Q_n: n*2^(n-1).

clusters.title: Formulate the LP from the passage: objective
clusters.technique: Objective coefficient = cost/profit per unit of each product times variable (12x+20y for diet; 30x+50y for cloth).

clusters.title: Formulate the LP from the passage: constraints
clusters.technique: One constraint per resource/nutrient; coefficient matrix columns are products. Diet = '>=' constraints, production = '<=' constraints.
clusters.what_changes: Passage values and direction of inequalities.

clusters.title: Write the dual of the passage LP
clusters.technique: Primal min with >= constraints => dual max with <= constraints, RHS of dual = primal costs, dual objective uses primal RHS, A is transposed.

clusters.title: Evaluate the passage LP at corner points (optimum value/solution)
clusters.technique: Compute intersection points of constraints, evaluate objective at feasible vertices, choose max/min.

clusters.title: Graphical LP solution
clusters.technique: Plot constraints, list feasible vertices and evaluate objective. For feasibility questions substitute each point into all constraints.

clusters.title: Simplex / dual simplex iterations
clusters.technique: Entering variable: largest positive Cj-Zj (max). Leaving: min ratio. Dual simplex: leaving row = most negative RHS.
clusters.skip_note: Both reduce to one tableau pivot.

clusters.title: LP duality theorems and rules
clusters.technique: Equality constraint in max primal => unrestricted dual variable; weak/strong duality; optimal tableau gives dual solution.

clusters.title: Group theory statement-check
clusters.technique: Facts: identity and inverse unique; element order divides |G|; even-order group has element of order 2; (xy)^2=x^2y^2 for all x,y implies abelian but x^3=1 does not; finite closed subset is a subgroup; group has at least one element.
clusters.what_changes: Which of A-D statements are listed.

clusters.title: Semigroup property reasoning
clusters.technique: Use the given hypothesis to force identities; two-element semigroup with a*a=b: b*b=b.

clusters.title: Homomorphism and automorphism of integer/real groups
clusters.technique: Kernel decides injectivity; image decides surjectivity; Aut(Z,+)={x->x, x->-x}.

clusters.title: Unknown-base arithmetic equation
clusters.technique: Expand each number in its base as polynomial in b, set equal, solve and check digit validity.

clusters.title: Radix and valid digit questions
clusters.technique: Digits must be smaller than base; for a quadratic with roots in base b, use sum/product of roots.

clusters.title: Euler/Fermat/modular computation
clusters.technique: phi(n)=n*prod(1-1/p); a^phi(n) = 1 mod n; Fermat a^(p-1)=1 mod p (not a^p=1); repeated squaring.

clusters.title: Poisson probability of zero arrivals
clusters.technique: P(0)=e^(-lambda t); convert rate to the time window (30/hr for 40 min => 20).

clusters.title: Full joint distribution table: marginal/conditional/union
clusters.technique: Add matching cells for marginals; P(A|B)=P(A and B)/P(B); P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B).
clusters.what_changes: Event asked from the same 8-cell table.
clusters.skip_note: Same table method; nov2021_q60 includes all steps.

clusters.title: Probability of numbers divisible by 2 or 5
clusters.technique: Inclusion-exclusion: 1/2+1/5-1/10 = 3/5.
clusters.skip_note: Same answer for any range multiple of 10.

clusters.title: Elementary probability with balls/coins
clusters.technique: Favourable/total with combinations: C(6,2)C(4,2)/C(10,4)=3/7.

examiner_mindset: Favourite format is the multi-select 'which of A-E are true' or Match-the-list: about a third of the unit uses these, so you must know every statement of a fact bank, not just one.

Recent papers re-use statement sets almost verbatim: Dec 2023 q42 and June 2024 (Cancelled) q22 share the same quantifier statements; Nov 2021 q27 and Dec 2024 q69 are the same planarity task; Dec 2023 q1 and June 2025 q27 differ only in the range (100 vs 200).

Passage blocks of five questions recur: Nov 2021 q56-60 (joint probability), Dec 2023 q91-95 (diet LP) and June 2024 Cancelled q91-95 (cloth LP). Each LP passage follows the same sequence: objective, constraints, dual, corner points, optimum.
Logic is the biggest topic (34 of 181) and almost always from the same toolbox: equivalences, quantifier truth in integers, negation, translation. Truth tables are not asked directly.

Typical distractors: converse vs contrapositive, distributing implication over AND/OR wrongly, Fermat's a^p=1 instead of a^(p-1)=1, Dirac's n/2 replaced by n/3, empty set vs {empty set}, an equivalence relation missing one property.

Difficulty is mostly easy-to-moderate recall; heavy computations (simplex tableaux, dual simplex) are rare and mostly in 2018-2019. After 2022 the examiner prefers conceptual statement checking and ordering/matching items.
Number reuse: Poisson with 20-30 requests per hour, 2-or-5 divisibility, unknown base with (b-2), and the regular wheel graph show up repeatedly with changed numbers.

Cross-unit overlap: PERT/CPM, Poisson and Bayes overlap with OR and probability topics; Boolean algebra overlaps with digital logic; trees overlap with data structures; recurrences overlap with algorithm analysis.
He never asks lengthy proofs, rings/fields in depth, calculus or matrices here; numerical methods appear only twice (June 2024 Cancelled) and the algebra part is limited to groups and semigroups.
Graph theory frequency has dropped since 2023 (6 questions in the last 6 papers vs 15 in the first 9) while LP and algebraic structures are rising.

clusters.title: Instruction cycle order
clusters.technique: Fetch instruction -> decode -> (calculate effective address) -> fetch operand -> execute. Check whether the option set includes the EA/operand steps; for register path PC->MAR->Memory->MBR->IR.
clusters.what_changes: Wording (A-E lettering vs I-III numbering), whether EA and operand fetch steps are included, and the MAR/MBR/PC register-level version.
clusters.skip_note: All five are the same fetch-decode-EA-operand-execute sequence; know it once and the option order is the only thing to read.

clusters.title: Instruction format field widths
clusters.technique: Address bits = log2(words); register bits = log2(#registers); mode/indirect bit = 1; opcode = word length - all other fields.
clusters.what_changes: Memory size, number of registers, number of mode bits.
clusters.skip_note: Same subtraction-of-fields calculation; only numbers differ.

clusters.title: Basic computer program trace
clusters.technique: Execute line by line with Mano basic-computer semantics (CLA, ADD, INC, CMA, AND, BUN, STA); track AC in hex.
clusters.skip_note: Same tracing routine; solve one and the other is only more arithmetic.

clusters.title: Basic computer instruction type encoding
clusters.technique: Mano format: mode bit I + 3-bit opcode + 12-bit address. Opcode 000-110 = memory reference; I=0,opcode 111 = register reference; I=1,opcode 111 = I/O reference. Register-ref mnemonics: SZA, SNA, SPA, CLA, CMA, INC; I/O: SKI, SKO.
clusters.what_changes: Asks to classify opcode/mode pairs or match skip/register mnemonics.
clusters.skip_note: Both test the same Mano instruction-set table.

clusters.title: RISC versus CISC
clusters.technique: RISC: load/store only memory access, fixed-length, single-cycle, pipelining friendly, hardwired. CISC: many addressing modes, variable length, microprogrammed.

clusters.title: Addressing modes facts and effective address
clusters.technique: Immediate: operand in instruction; direct: EA=address field; indirect: EA=M[address] (2 memory refs); register: 0 memory refs; indexed: EA=address+XR; register indirect: EA=R. Fastest = register/immediate.
clusters.what_changes: Conceptual statement vs numeric EA computation.
clusters.skip_note: One table of modes with EA formulas answers all six.

clusters.title: 8085 instruction set and addressing
clusters.technique: Memorise 8085 categories: DAA arithmetic; LXI, MVI, MOV data transfer; JMP branch/program control; RST interrupt. Addressing: STA/LDA direct, MOV A,M register indirect, MOV A,B register, MVI immediate.

clusters.title: Memory capacity, address lines and chip count
clusters.technique: Capacity = 2^(address lines) x data lines. Address lines = log2(words). Chips = total bits / chip bits; byte-addressable vs word-addressable changes address bits.
clusters.skip_note: All reduce to capacity = 2^n x m and its inverse.

clusters.title: Direct-mapped cache address fields
clusters.technique: Address bits = tag + line/index + word offset. Offset = log2(block size), line = log2(#lines), tag = rest. Main memory = 2^(tag+index), cache = 2^index.
clusters.what_changes: Given fields -> sizes, or given sizes -> fields.

clusters.title: Average memory access time
clusters.technique: T = h*Tc + (1-h)*Tm; for two levels apply recursively from the lowest level.

clusters.title: Memory hierarchy speed ordering
clusters.technique: Fastest to slowest: Registers > Cache (SRAM) > DRAM > SSD > Hard disk > Optical > Magnetic tape. Reverse for access time vs speed.
clusters.what_changes: Ascending vs descending order, subset of devices.
clusters.skip_note: Same single ordering; read whether asked ascending or descending.

clusters.title: Primary versus secondary memory statements
clusters.technique: CPU accesses primary memory directly, secondary only via I/O; primary holds active programs; secondary is backup/bulk storage.
clusters.what_changes: Question asks true in one shift and false in the other.

clusters.title: Memory types and technology facts
clusters.technique: DRAM: slower, denser, cheaper, needs refresh; SRAM: faster, used for cache. CMOS chip on motherboard = ROM per the answer key; main memory = RAM+ROM; CAM = content search in parallel; access time definition.
clusters.skip_note: All are one-line factual recalls from the same memory-type notes.

clusters.title: Cache coherence and write policies
clusters.technique: Write-through updates cache and memory; write-back updates cache only (dirty bit). Coherence solved by snoopy controllers or by not caching shared data.

clusters.title: Cache terminology and mapping
clusters.technique: Mappings: direct, associative, set-associative. Dirty bit = block modified after loading. Hit ratio is the key performance metric. Mapping = transforming main-memory blocks to cache lines.
clusters.skip_note: One-line definitions from the cache chapter.

clusters.title: K-map simplification
clusters.technique: Plot minterms, group 1s in powers of 2 (largest groups, wrap-around), treat don't cares as 1 only if they enlarge a group, write each group as product of unchanged variables. Alternatively test each option by plugging minterms.
clusters.what_changes: 3 or 4 variables, with/without don't cares, or steps order.
clusters.skip_note: Same grouping skill; do one 4-var with don't cares and one 3-var.

clusters.title: Boolean simplification and identities
clusters.technique: Apply absorption (x+xy=x), idempotent, domination, complement laws and XOR identities (A xor 1 = A', A xor 0 = A, A xor A = 0). Sum of A'B+AB'+AB = A+B.
clusters.what_changes: Expression to simplify or identity to verify.

clusters.title: Complement of Boolean function
clusters.technique: De Morgan: complement = swap AND/OR and complement each literal (dual and complement variables).

clusters.title: Logic gate properties
clusters.technique: NAND/NOR universal; XOR odd function (1 when odd number of 1s); XNOR output 1 for equal inputs; with inputs 00 NAND=1,NOR=1,XNOR=1,XOR=0. 2421 and excess-3 are self-complementing; buffer = amplification.
clusters.what_changes: Match-list or option-based gate truth tables.

clusters.title: Decoder, encoder and multiplexer functions
clusters.technique: Decoder n -> 2^n; encoder 2^n -> n (priority encoder resolves multiple inputs); mux 2^n -> 1; demux 1 -> 2^n. Half adder = 2-bit addition.
clusters.what_changes: Match-list or identify circuit from equations.

clusters.title: Combinational versus sequential circuits
clusters.technique: Combinational: output depends on present input only, no memory, no feedback, no clock. Sequential: has memory/feedback, clocked. FF, counter, register sequential; mux, decoder, adder combinational.

clusters.title: Counters
clusters.technique: Cascaded counters: states multiply (MOD-2 x MOD-5 = 10). JK with J=K=1 toggling with output clocking next = ripple (asynchronous). Ring counter N states; decade counter 0-9; synchronous = common clock.

clusters.title: Flip-flop basics
clusters.technique: Flip-flop stores one bit. SR: S=R=0 no change, S=R=1 invalid. Register = group of FFs.

clusters.title: Interrupt service routine sequence
clusters.technique: ISR order: save registers -> check which flag is set -> service device -> restore registers -> turn interrupt facility on -> return.

clusters.title: I/O procedure ordering
clusters.technique: Programmed input: read status register -> check flag -> read data register -> transfer to memory. DMA: request -> grant -> transfer -> release. Complexity order: I/O module < DMA < channel < I/O processor.
clusters.skip_note: Each is one memorised ordered list.

clusters.title: Isolated versus memory-mapped I/O
clusters.technique: Isolated: separate address space and special IN/OUT instructions. Memory-mapped: shares addresses and control signals with memory, uses normal load/store.

clusters.title: I/O transfer techniques
clusters.technique: Techniques: programmed, interrupt-driven, DMA (also IOP/channel). Handshaking uses two opposite control signals. I/O write = memory/CPU to device.

clusters.title: Interrupt types and handling
clusters.technique: Internal (stack overflow, invalid opcode), external (timer, I/O), software (supervisor call), machine check. Handler address not fixed (vectored); dedicated interrupt request line.

clusters.title: Two's complement representation and arithmetic
clusters.technique: -N in n bits = 2^n - N (invert and add 1). Overflow in addition iff both operands same sign and result sign differs. n-bit signed range -2^(n-1)..2^(n-1)-1. Subtraction = add 2's complement.

clusters.title: Number base conversion
clusters.technique: Group bits in 4s for hex, 3s for octal; fractional parts multiply by 2 repeatedly; negative fixed point = 2's complement of the positive pattern.

clusters.title: Gray and BCD-type codes
clusters.technique: Gray: g = b xor (b>>1), successive codes differ by one bit. Self-complementing: 2421, excess-3 (not 8421).

clusters.title: Amdahl's law speedup
clusters.technique: Speedup = 1/((1-f)+f/s). With p processors: T = serial + parallel/p.
clusters.what_changes: Fraction and factor, or cycle counts.

clusters.title: Multiprocessor architecture facts
clusters.technique: Multiprocessor: one OS, shared memory; multicomputer: separate computers on communication lines. NUMA: single address space, remote access via load/store and slower than local. Crossbar is non-blocking.

clusters.title: Pipeline speedup and total time
clusters.technique: Pipelined time = (k+n-1) x clock (clock = max stage delay + register delay); non-pipelined = n x t. Speedup = n*t_np / ((k+n-1)*tp).
clusters.what_changes: Task count, stage delays, speedup vs total time.

clusters.title: Microinstruction format size
clusters.technique: Bits = sum of fields: each field ceil(log2 options); address field = log2(control memory words).

examiner_mindset: Questions are overwhelmingly factual recall, ordered-sequence and match-the-list formats; roughly 70% need no calculation, so breadth beats depth.

Ordering questions (instruction cycle, ISR steps, memory hierarchy, DMA steps, arithmetic pipeline) recur with the options shuffled; the instruction cycle order alone appeared in 5 papers and the ISR sequence twice.
Exact repeats are common across shifts/papers: Dec 2022 Shift I/II primary-vs-secondary statements, and ISR sequence in Dec 2024 and June 2024 Cancelled.

Calculation questions reuse the same formula with new numbers: pipeline (k+n-1) formula (4 papers), Amdahl (3 papers), direct-mapped fields (2), average access time (2), instruction-field bit widths (2), microinstruction size (2).
Statement-combination and 'which are NOT' options punish half-knowledge; distractors are swapped definitions (write-through vs write-back, isolated vs memory-mapped).
Digital logic is tested through K-map and Boolean simplification at medium difficulty; every paper has about one such question and the answer is checkable by plugging minterms.

Cross-unit overlap: Boolean/K-map and gates feed Unit 2 only here but number systems and 8085/basic-computer content appear in OS/programming style questions elsewhere; digital-logic tags are sometimes assigned to memory-sizing questions.

Never asked so far: cache replacement (LRU/FIFO) numericals, hazard types/forwarding, CPI/MIPS computation, Booth multiplication, hit-ratio with miss-penalty tables, virtual memory addressing. Pipeline hazards are a likely future gap.
Difficulty is mostly 1-2 on a 3-point scale; the only multi-step items are IEEE-754 conversion, 2-level cache time, program traces and the DRAM refresh calculation.
Recent papers (2023-2025) lean toward ordered-list and statement formats in CPU, I/O and memory hierarchy, with fewer pure numericals.

formulas.name: Instruction word bit allocation
formulas.formula: word bits = mode/indirect + opcode + register code + address; address bits = log2(#words); register bits = log2(#registers)
formulas.note: Opcode = remainder after other fields; 512K words -> 19 address bits, 256K -> 18.

formulas.name: Mano basic-computer instruction types
formulas.formula: I + 3-bit opcode + 12-bit address; opcode 000-110 memory ref; I=0 & 111 register ref; I=1 & 111 I/O ref
formulas.note: Register ref: CLA, CMA, INC, SZA, SNA, SPA; I/O: INP, OUT, SKI, SKO; ISZ is memory-reference.

formulas.name: Instruction cycle
formulas.formula: Fetch -> Decode -> Calculate EA -> Fetch operand -> Execute; fetch: PC->MAR->Memory->MBR->IR

formulas.name: Effective address by mode
formulas.formula: immediate: operand=field; direct: EA=A; indirect: EA=M[A]; register: EA=R; reg indirect: EA=[R]; indexed: EA=A+XR; relative: EA=PC+A
formulas.note: Indirect needs 2 memory refs for operand; register needs 0.

formulas.name: Memory capacity
formulas.formula: bits = 2^(address lines) x data lines; address lines = log2(words); chips = total / chip size
formulas.note: Word-addressable: divide bytes by word size first.

formulas.name: Direct-mapped cache fields
formulas.formula: address = tag | line | offset; offset = log2(block), line = log2(#lines); main memory = 2^(tag+line) words
formulas.note: Cache size = 2^line index (x block size for total).

formulas.name: Average access time
formulas.formula: T = h*Tc + (1-h)*Tm (recursive for multi-level)
formulas.note: Check whether the question gives Tm inclusive of cache probe.

formulas.name: Memory hierarchy speed order
formulas.formula: Registers > Cache(SRAM) > DRAM > SSD > HDD > Optical > Tape

formulas.name: Write policies
formulas.formula: write-through: cache+memory updated; write-back: cache only, dirty bit marks modified block

formulas.name: DRAM refresh overhead
formulas.formula: fraction = (rows x refresh time per row) / refresh interval

formulas.name: K-map rules
formulas.formula: group 1s in powers of 2, wrap edges, don't care used only if it enlarges a group; each group = product of constant variables
formulas.note: Shortcut: test each option against the minterm list.

formulas.name: Boolean identities
formulas.formula: x+xy=x, x+x=x, x+1=1, x+0=x, x+x'y=x+y, A'B+AB'+AB=A+B, A xor 1 = A', A xor A = 0

formulas.name: De Morgan
formulas.formula: (A+B)' = A'B', (AB)' = A'+B'; complement of SOP = product of complemented sums
formulas.note: Complement every literal and swap AND/OR.

formulas.name: Gate outputs for inputs 00
formulas.formula: NAND=1, NOR=1, XOR=0, XNOR=1; XOR is odd function

formulas.name: Decoder/mux/encoder sizes
formulas.formula: decoder n -> 2^n; encoder 2^n -> n; mux 2^n -> 1; demux 1 -> 2^n; k arbiters need priority encoder of k lines (ceil(log2 k) outputs) and decoder back
formulas.note: Priority encoder resolves simultaneous inputs; 5 arbiters -> 8x3 and 3x8.

formulas.name: Common bus
formulas.formula: n registers of m bits -> m multiplexers each n x 1

formulas.name: Cascaded counters
formulas.formula: states = product of moduli (MOD-2 followed by MOD-5 = 10); N-bit ring counter has N states
formulas.note: Ripple counter = output of one FF clocks next.

formulas.name: SR flip-flop
formulas.formula: S=R=0 hold; S=1,R=0 set; S=0,R=1 reset; S=R=1 invalid

formulas.name: ISR / programmed I/O orders
formulas.formula: ISR: save regs, check flag, service, restore regs, enable interrupts; programmed input: read status, check flag, read data, store to memory; DMA: request, grant, transfer, release
formulas.note: Interrupt enable is turned on near the end.

formulas.name: Isolated vs memory-mapped I/O
formulas.formula: isolated: separate address spaces + IN/OUT; memory-mapped: shared address space, ordinary load/store
formulas.note: Memory-mapped uses same control signals as memory.

formulas.name: Two's complement
formulas.formula: -N = 2^n - N = invert + 1; range -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1)-1; overflow iff operands same sign and result sign differs

formulas.name: Base conversion
formulas.formula: hex digit = 4 bits, octal digit = 3 bits; fraction: multiply by 2
formulas.note: Regroup binary from the radix point outward.

formulas.name: Gray code
formulas.formula: g_i = b_i xor b_(i+1); MSB unchanged; adjacent codes differ in 1 bit

formulas.name: Self-complementing codes
formulas.formula: 2421 and excess-3 (and excess-3 Gray per key) are self-complementing; 8421 is not

formulas.name: IEEE-754 single precision
formulas.formula: 1 sign | 8 exponent (bias 127) | 23 mantissa; value = (-1)^s x 1.m x 2^(e-127)

formulas.name: Arithmetic shift
formulas.formula: ASR keeps sign bit and divides by 2; ASL multiplies by 2
formulas.note: Logical shift does not preserve sign.

formulas.name: Amdahl's law
formulas.formula: Speedup = 1 / ((1-f) + f/s); with p processors: T = T_serial + T_parallel/p

formulas.name: Vector processor cycles
formulas.formula: cycles = (elements / lanes) as keyed; x per-op cycles only if specified as a pipeline
formulas.note: The key gives 64 = 1024/16, ignoring the 5-cycle latency.

formulas.name: Pipeline time and speedup
formulas.formula: T_pipe = (k+n-1) x t_clock; S = n*t_np / ((k+n-1)*t_clock); max speedup -> k
formulas.note: t_clock = max stage delay + latch delay; speedup never equals k exactly.

formulas.name: Pipeline speedup with different CPI
formulas.formula: speedup = (avg unpipelined time) / (clock + overhead)
formulas.note: Unpipelined avg CPI 4.4 x 10 ns = 44 ns; pipelined 11 ns -> 4x.

formulas.name: Microinstruction size
formulas.formula: sum of ceil(log2(options)) over fields + address bits (log2 control memory)
formulas.note: 15 ops -> 4 bits; 4 status bits -> 2 bits CD; 128 words -> 7 bits.

formulas.name: Flynn taxonomy
formulas.formula: SISD, SIMD, MISD, MIMD; complexity SISD < SIMD < MIMD

clusters.title: Bit-loop functions (popcount / power-of-2 / bit reversal)
clusters.technique: Trace n&1 and n>>=1 on a small number; popcount counts 1-bits; a stray "counter = 1" in the return makes the answer a constant test. For reversal, build b = 2b + (a&1).
clusters.what_changes: Language (C, C++, Java), return expression, and which property (count of 1s, power of 2, reversed bits) is asked.

clusters.title: Recursive Java f(m,n) geometric series
clusters.technique: Unroll the recursion: result = m/n added to the recursive term; terms form a geometric series a/(1-r); plug values.
clusters.skip_note: Identical function skeleton, only constants change; solve the Nov 2020 one and the series idea transfers.

clusters.title: Recursion call-counting in C

clusters.title: Pointer arithmetic and indexing output
clusters.technique: Rewrite everything as *(base+offset); p++ post-increments after use; &arr+1 jumps the whole array; ptr[i]=*(ptr+i) and negative indices are legal.
clusters.what_changes: Array contents, offset expressions, whether &arr, p++ or p[-i] is used.
clusters.skip_note: All four are *(p+k) bookkeeping; master the &arr+1 and *p++ rules and the rest are mechanical.

clusters.title: Legal and illegal pointer operations
clusters.technique: Allowed: ptr+-int, ptr-ptr (gives int), assigning &var. Illegal: ptr+ptr, ptr*int, ptr/int, assigning int to pointer without cast, &constant.
clusters.what_changes: Which operation or statement is offered as the trap.
clusters.skip_note: One rule table (pointer legality) answers all four.

clusters.title: Pointer concept statements (what pointers can/cannot do)
clusters.technique: Pointers store addresses, can point to pointers, access arrays, simulate call by reference, build dynamic structures; they are not auto-dereferenced.
clusters.what_changes: Wording of which capability is true/false.
clusters.skip_note: Pure fact-recall of the same list.

clusters.title: Multi-dimensional array to pointer expression
clusters.technique: a[i][j][k] = *(*(*(a+i)+j)+k); count dereference levels equal to dimensions.
clusters.skip_note: Same identity; distractors only mis-place parentheses.

clusters.title: Decoding C declarations (function pointer / typedef)
clusters.technique: Read declarations inside-out: int (*f)(int,int) is a pointer to function; typedef (*(*arrfptr[3])())[10] is array of 3 pointers to functions returning pointer to array of 10.

clusters.title: Struct/union memory layout, padding and endianness
clusters.technique: Align each member to a multiple of its size, pad struct to multiple of max alignment, union size = largest member; little endian value = b1*256+b0.
clusters.what_changes: Member list, machine word size, or byte values.
clusters.skip_note: All three are byte-layout arithmetic; do the padding one and the union one.

clusters.title: Operator precedence ordering
clusters.technique: Order: shift > relational (<,>,>=) > equality (==) > && > || > ?: > assignment (+=); arithmetic binds tightest here.

clusters.title: Loop tracing with small counters
clusters.technique: Write variable table per iteration; watch break, step sizes and the loop test; Euclid-by-subtraction ends at gcd.
clusters.what_changes: Loop bounds, break placement, shadowed variable, or log-count form.
clusters.skip_note: All five are hand-trace of 3-8 iterations; do the shadowing and the break ones.

clusters.title: One-line expression gotchas (ternary, comma, macro, literals)
clusters.technique: Evaluate exactly as the compiler: ternary picks branch, comma yields last value, macro expands textually (b+2*b+2), 0x is hex and leading 0 is octal.
clusters.skip_note: Each tests one language rule; learn the four rules once.

clusters.title: Ordering process steps
clusters.technique: Know the canonical sequence: do-while is init -> body -> test; viewing pipeline is world scene -> viewing coords -> normalized -> device; runtime is statement -> compile -> type -> allocate -> deallocate.
clusters.skip_note: Sequence questions are common-sense rank ordering from the option patterns.

clusters.title: C file-handling functions and steps
clusters.technique: fopen -> check error -> read/write -> fclose; fseek sets position, ftell gives position, rewind goes to start, feof tests end.

clusters.title: Constructor facts in C++

clusters.title: Polymorphism, virtual functions and inheritance benefits
clusters.technique: Run-time polymorphism = virtual functions + base-class interface; pure virtual (=0) makes a class abstract; overriding is late binding, overloading is early binding.
clusters.what_changes: Direct definition vs match vs T/F.
clusters.skip_note: Same definition set tested five ways.

clusters.title: Access control: protected inheritance, friend, scope resolution
clusters.technique: Protected inheritance makes public/protected base members protected in derived; objects outside cannot access them; friend breaks encapsulation without being a member.

clusters.title: Call by value vs reference tracing
clusters.technique: Value copies: swap on copies does nothing; reference/pointer swaps change originals; swapping char* locally vs via char** differ.
clusters.what_changes: Language syntax and type being swapped.
clusters.skip_note: One parameter-passing model solves all five.

clusters.title: Display and colour terminology

clusters.what_changes: Scale factors and whether origin or fixed point.

clusters.title: Homogeneous 3x3 transformation matrices
clusters.technique: Read the matrix: translation in last column, scale on diagonal, shear off-diagonal; compose right-to-left; reflection about x-axis is diag(1,-1).
clusters.skip_note: Same matrix reading skill; do the shear one.

clusters.title: Projection properties (perspective, parallel, oblique)
clusters.technique: Perspective: farther is smaller, parallel lines converge, divide by z, needs homogeneous coords; orthographic is affine and keeps parallels; cavalier no foreshortening, cabinet half.

clusters.title: Clipping algorithms identification
clusters.technique: Line clipping: Cohen-Sutherland, Liang-Barsky, Nicholl-Lee-Nicholl; polygon clipping: Sutherland-Hodgman (convex window); clipping removes outside parts.

formulas.name: Frame buffer size
formulas.formula: bytes = X * Y * bits_per_pixel / 8 (640*480*12/8 = 460800 B = 450 KB)
formulas.note: Divide by 8 for bytes, then 1024 for KB; 1 MP is ~1e6 pixels and 1-bit images need 1/8 byte.

formulas.name: Colour lookup table size
formulas.formula: LUT = 2^bits_per_pixel entries * (3*8 bits) = 2^bits * 3 bytes
formulas.note: Frame buffer 10 bpp: LUT 1024 entries * 3 bytes = 2^10 + 2^11 bytes.

formulas.name: Refresh rate
formulas.formula: rate = 1 / (pixels * access time) (640*480*200 ns = 61.4 ms, about 16 fps)
formulas.note: Pixels count first; 1 bit depth does not change per-pixel time.

formulas.name: Aspect-ratio resize
formulas.note: Keep ratio, scale both sides by the same factor.

formulas.name: 2D scaling
formulas.formula: x' = sx*x, y' = sy*y; matrix diag(sx, sy)
formulas.note: Factor > 1 enlarges, < 1 shrinks; applied about origin.

formulas.name: Scaling about fixed point F
formulas.formula: P' = F + s(P - F)
formulas.note: F stays unchanged; compute each vertex difference from F.

formulas.name: Homogeneous 2D matrices
formulas.note: Composite M = M_last ... M_first; the rightmost matrix acts first.

formulas.name: Reflection about X axis
formulas.formula: diag(1,-1); determinant -1, so not a rotation
formulas.note: Reflection is not a rotation matrix; y-axis reflection is diag(-1,1).

formulas.name: Perspective division
formulas.formula: x' = x/z, y' = y/z via homogeneous w; non-linear in Cartesian, linear only in homogeneous coordinates
formulas.note: Parallel lines converge except those parallel to the view plane; parallel projection = viewer at infinity.

formulas.name: Orthographic projection
formulas.formula: Affine: preserves parallel lines, no size change with depth
formulas.note: Cavalier: no foreshortening; cabinet: half-scale depth; both oblique.

formulas.name: Cubic Bezier
formulas.formula: P(t)=sum B_i P_i, with P(0)=P0, P(1)=P3, P(1/2)=(P0+3P1+3P2+P3)/8; 4 control points, inside convex hull
formulas.note: Interpolates only end points; tangent at ends along P1-P0 and P3-P2.

formulas.name: Phong specular term
formulas.formula: I_s = k_s (R . V)^n  (reflected vector and view vector)
formulas.note: Not the normal and light vector; that is the diffuse term.

formulas.name: Clipping facts
formulas.formula: Cohen-Sutherland: accept if both outcodes 0000, reject if AND != 0; Sutherland-Hodgman clips polygons against convex window; a triangle clipped by a rectangle gives at most 7 sides
formulas.note: Sutherland-Hodgman is polygon clipping, not line clipping.

formulas.name: Row-major 3D address
formulas.formula: addr(A[r][s][t]) = base + w*(b*c*r + c*s + t) for int A[a][b][c]
formulas.note: First index multiplies b*c; the leading dimension a never appears.

formulas.name: Array/pointer identity
formulas.formula: a[i] = *(a+i); a[i][j][k] = *(*(*(a+i)+j)+k); ptr[-1] legal; &arr+1 moves past whole array
formulas.note: Pointer arithmetic scales by element size.

formulas.name: Pointer operation legality
formulas.formula: ptr +/- int -> ptr; ptr - ptr -> int; ptr + ptr, ptr*int, ptr/int illegal; int to pointer needs a cast
formulas.note: Option "pointer - pointer -> pointer" is the usual trap.

formulas.name: Struct alignment
formulas.formula: member offset multiple of its size; struct size multiple of largest member alignment; union size = largest member
formulas.note: Add padding after members as well as before.

formulas.name: Little-endian value
formulas.formula: two-byte value = byte1*256 + byte0 (5, 2 gives 517)

formulas.name: C operator precedence
formulas.formula: arithmetic > shift > relational (<,>,>=) > equality (==) > && > || > ?: > assignment (=,+=) > comma

formulas.name: Macro expansion
formulas.formula: SQR(x) = (x*x) with x = b+2 expands to b+2*b+2 = 11 for b=3

formulas.name: Number literals
formulas.formula: 0x10 = 16, leading 0 means octal: 010 = 8

formulas.name: Bit loop
formulas.formula: while(n){c+=n&1; n>>=1;} counts set bits; N&(N-1)==0 tests power of 2
formulas.note: Check the return statement for assignment typos.

formulas.name: Loop iteration count
formulas.formula: while(p<b){p*=a;x++;} gives x = ceil(log_a b)
formulas.note: Ceil not floor because exit needs p >= b.

formulas.name: Geometric series sum
formulas.formula: S = a/(1-r), |r|<1 (recursive Java f sums to 0.2)
formulas.note: Check the base case before summing.

formulas.name: Constructor/destructor order
formulas.formula: Constructors run base -> derived; destructors derived -> base; virtual destructor needed for delete through base pointer
formulas.note: Without virtual, only the base destructor runs.

formulas.name: Parameter passing
formulas.formula: By value: copy, caller unchanged; by reference / pointer: original changed; swapping char* needs char**
formulas.note: f1(char*,char*) swap has no caller effect.

formulas.name: XML validity
formulas.formula: valid XML => also well-formed (not the reverse); XML is case sensitive; namespaces provide globally unique names

formulas.name: Visibility
formulas.formula: Back-face culling: object space; Painter and z-buffer: image/depth-order; collinear with viewpoint means nearer obscures farther

formulas.name: Attribute closure
formulas.formula: X+ = X plus attributes derived by repeatedly applying FDs; X is a superkey iff X+ = all attributes
formulas.note: Attributes never on any RHS must be in every key

formulas.name: Candidate key
formulas.formula: Minimal superkey; alternate key = candidate not chosen as primary

formulas.name: Minimal cover
formulas.formula: Single-attribute RHS; no extraneous LHS attribute; no redundant FD
formulas.note: Redundant FD = derivable from the rest

formulas.name: 2NF
formulas.formula: No non-prime attribute depends on a proper subset of a candidate key

formulas.name: 3NF
formulas.formula: For each X->A: X is a superkey or A is prime

formulas.name: BCNF
formulas.formula: For each nontrivial X->A: X is a superkey
formulas.note: BCNF => 3NF => 2NF => 1NF; may lose dependency preservation; any 2-attribute relation is in BCNF

formulas.name: 4NF / 5NF
formulas.formula: 4NF: every nontrivial MVD has a superkey LHS; 5NF: every join dependency is implied by candidate keys

formulas.name: Lossless binary decomposition
formulas.formula: R1 intersect R2 -> R1 or R1 intersect R2 -> R2
formulas.note: Also check each original FD is preserved in some fragment

formulas.name: 3NF guarantee
formulas.formula: 3NF synthesis is always lossless and dependency preserving; BCNF is lossless but may not preserve

formulas.name: Cross product and join size
formulas.formula: Cross product: degree d1+d2, tuples n1*n2; natural join max tuples n1*n2, min 0
formulas.note: Outer joins add unmatched tuples (right outer >= |right relation|)

formulas.name: Relational division
formulas.formula: pi(x,y)(R) / pi(y)(S) gives x paired with every y

formulas.name: Degree and cardinality
formulas.formula: Degree = number of attributes; cardinality = number of tuples

formulas.name: Referential integrity
formulas.formula: Insert into referencing and delete from referenced relation can violate; ON DELETE CASCADE deletes referencing tuples

formulas.name: B+ tree leaf order
formulas.formula: p*(key + record ptr) + block ptr <= B so p = floor((B - Pb)/(K+Pr))
formulas.note: B=1024,K=9,Pr=7,Pb=6 gives 63; key for B-tree item was (57,53)

formulas.name: Conflicting operations
formulas.formula: Different transactions, same item, at least one write
formulas.note: Cycle in precedence graph => not conflict serializable

formulas.name: Serializability hierarchy
formulas.formula: Conflict serializable => view serializable; Thomas write rule only view serializable

formulas.name: Concurrency protocols
formulas.formula: 2PL may deadlock; strict 2PL cascadeless; conservative 2PL and timestamp ordering deadlock-free; tree protocol deadlock-free

formulas.name: Phantom problem
formulas.formula: Caused by insertions; prevented by index locking or predicate locking

formulas.name: ACID
formulas.formula: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
formulas.note: Deadlock-freedom is not part of ACID

formulas.name: Transaction states
formulas.formula: Active -> partially committed -> committed; active/partially committed -> failed -> aborted
formulas.note: From active: partially committed or failed

formulas.name: Irrecoverable schedule
formulas.formula: Tj reads data written by Ti and commits before Ti commits
formulas.note: Cascadeless needs reads only of committed data

formulas.name: DDL vs DML
formulas.formula: DDL: CREATE, ALTER, DROP; DML: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

formulas.name: WHERE vs HAVING
formulas.formula: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation

formulas.name: COUNT variants
formulas.formula: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(col) ignores NULL; COUNT(DISTINCT col) counts distinct values
formulas.note: Missing join condition gives Cartesian product (nov2020_q97)

formulas.name: Top-k correlated query
formulas.formula: where (select count(*) from book where price > B.price) < k lists the k most expensive

formulas.name: varchar vs char
formulas.formula: varchar uses actual length; char(n) is padded to n

formulas.name: Hadoop roles
formulas.formula: NameNode = master, DataNode = worker

formulas.name: Design phases
formulas.formula: Requirements, conceptual, logical, physical

formulas.name: ER-to-relational
formulas.formula: Entity -> table; multivalued attribute -> separate table; M:N -> own table; many-to-one r1 to r2: Pk(r1) -> Pk(r2)

clusters.title: SSTF seek-time/head-movement on a request queue
clusters.technique: Sort out nearest-first order: from the head repeatedly pick the pending request with smallest |difference|; add the gaps (multiply by ms per cylinder if asked). Draw the visiting order on one line.
clusters.what_changes: Request list, head start, cylinder count and ms/cylinder. june2019_q41 and june2023_q78 are the same queue (4,34,10,7,19,73,2,15,6,20 from 50 = 119).
clusters.skip_note: If you can run SSTF once on june2023_q78 the other three are only different numbers.

clusters.title: Total head movement for FCFS / SCAN / C-SCAN / C-LOOK
clusters.technique: FCFS = sum of consecutive gaps. SCAN goes to the disk end then reverses; C-SCAN goes to the end then jumps to 0 (jump counted in the usual textbook answer) and continues; LOOK/C-LOOK turn at the last request, not the disk end.
clusters.what_changes: Algorithm, direction, start head, queue, disk size.
clusters.skip_note: Same single skill of tracing one policy; after solving the June 2025 queue under two policies the rest follow.

clusters.title: Identify the 2nd request served / the policy from a head graph
clusters.technique: Trace the policy order on the same queue: C-LOOK(right) serves increasing requests then jumps to the lowest; SCAN(left) serves decreasing requests first. For a graph, look for a jump back without touching the disk end = C-LOOK.
clusters.what_changes: Which policy and direction; asks order rather than total.
clusters.skip_note: Pure order-of-service tracing already trained by the head-movement cluster.

clusters.title: Disk capacity / geometry arithmetic
clusters.technique: capacity = surfaces x tracks x sectors/track x bytes/sector; cylinders = tracks per surface; sector-address bits = log2(total sectors).
clusters.what_changes: Which quantity is asked (capacity, track size, bits, sectors per track).
clusters.skip_note: All are multiplications of the same four parameters; do nov2020_q92 and the rest are the same product.

clusters.title: Rotational delay and data-transfer rate
clusters.technique: max rotational delay = 60/rpm s (avg = half); transfer rate = bytes per track x revolutions per second.
clusters.what_changes: rpm and which of the two is asked.
clusters.skip_note: Both come from the nov2020 passage disk; one rep suffices.

clusters.title: RAID level matching
clusters.technique: Memorise: 0 striping, 1 mirroring, 2 bit-level ECC (memory-style), 3 bit-interleaved parity, 4 block-interleaved parity, 5 block-interleaved distributed parity, 6 P+Q / Reed-Solomon.
clusters.what_changes: Pairing of levels with descriptions; wording of descriptions varies.
clusters.skip_note: Same table of RAID facts every time; learn it once.

clusters.title: File allocation methods and fragmentation
clusters.technique: Contiguous: external fragmentation, fast direct access. Linked: no external fragmentation, no direct access, pointer space. Indexed: direct + sequential, no external fragmentation, index-block overhead.
clusters.what_changes: Direction of question (which suffers / which advantages).

clusters.title: Paging address arithmetic (pages, frames, offset, page table size, internal fragmentation)
clusters.technique: pages = VA size/page size; offset bits = log2(page size); frames = PM size/page size; PT size = pages x entry size; internal fragmentation = unused part of last page.
clusters.what_changes: Memory sizes, page size, PTE size, which quantity asked.
clusters.skip_note: Nov 2021 passage gives all subparts; rest are variants of the same computation.

clusters.title: Effective access time with TLB
clusters.technique: EMAT = h(t+m) + (1-h)(t+2m) for single-level paging (t = TLB time, m = memory time).

clusters.title: Logical / virtual / physical address terminology
clusters.technique: Address in main memory = physical address; CPU-generated = logical (virtual); address space = logical/virtual set, memory space = physical set.

clusters.title: Count page faults on a reference string (FIFO / LRU / Optimal)
clusters.technique: Simulate frames in a table; FIFO evicts oldest loaded, LRU least recently used, Optimal the page used farthest in future. Count misses.
clusters.what_changes: Algorithm, frame count and reference string (and sometimes a difference between two algorithms).
clusters.skip_note: Mechanical simulation; practise on nov2020_q15 (FIFO and LRU) and the others are the same drill.

clusters.title: June 2023 passage: column-major vs row-major array traversal under LRU
clusters.technique: Pages hold rows of 1024 entries per page; column-wise traversal of 17 rows with 17 or fewer frames: count faults per column vs row-wise: 17 faults once, then hits.
clusters.what_changes: Subquestion (faults, hit ratio, ratio of faults).
clusters.skip_note: One passage; solving one sub-question gives all.

clusters.title: Effective access time with page faults / hit ratio
clusters.technique: EAT = (1-p)*m + p*(fault service time); with hit ratio h: h*t_primary + (1-h)*t_secondary.

clusters.title: Virtual memory conceptual statements
clusters.technique: Virtual memory increases effective capacity; program can be larger than RAM; not all pages need to be loaded; address translation for every logical address.

clusters.title: Order of page-replacement steps
clusters.technique: Find page on disk; if no free frame use algorithm to pick victim, write it back if dirty, update tables; read in desired page; restart instruction.

clusters.title: Linux interrupt protection level ordering
clusters.technique: Increasing priority: user mode < kernel system service routines < bottom half handlers < top half handlers.
clusters.what_changes: Only the lettering of the options.
clusters.skip_note: Identical question in Dec 2023 and June 2025.

clusters.title: I/O protection and interrupts
clusters.technique: I/O instructions are privileged; with memory-mapped I/O protection is by the OS (memory protection); I/O completion interrupts are different from a trap for protection.

clusters.title: Unix/Linux command facts
clusters.technique: wc -l counts lines; chmod -R a+x; lpr prints; user passwords/accounts in /etc/passwd; glob *.[ch].

clusters.title: Process-creation system calls (fork, exec, clone, kill, exit)
clusters.technique: fork creates child; exec loads new program; kill sends signal; exit terminates; clone gives selective sharing flags (Linux).

clusters.title: Match-the-following of OS terms
clusters.technique: Link each term to its area: Banker = resource allocation, demand paging = virtual memory, LFU = cache replacement, critical section = mutual exclusion, firmware = ROM, PCB = TCB, IPC = computational speedup.
clusters.skip_note: Examiner reuses the same standard pairings.

clusters.title: Preemptive SJF / SRTF waiting or turnaround time
clusters.technique: Draw the Gantt chart; at every arrival compare remaining times. TAT = CT - AT; WT = TAT - BT.
clusters.what_changes: Arrival and burst values; nov2021_q75 and july2018_q59 are near-identical sets.

clusters.title: Non-preemptive FCFS / SJF / HRRN metrics on one process set
clusters.technique: FCFS by arrival; SJF picks the smallest burst among arrived processes; HRRN ratio = (W+S)/S. Weighted turnaround = TAT/burst.
clusters.skip_note: Dec 2024 passage shares one table across sub-questions.

clusters.title: Priority scheduling average waiting / response time (non-preemptive)
clusters.technique: Order by priority (lower number first), then cumulative start times give waiting times.

clusters.title: Round-robin waiting/turnaround and maximum wait
clusters.technique: Simulate the queue with quantum q; waiting = completion - arrival - burst; worst-case wait for n processes = (n-1)q.

clusters.title: Scheduling theory statements (starvation, response time, quantum)
clusters.technique: SRTF and priority may starve; HRRN/aging fixes starvation; RR gives better response than FCFS; tiny quantum means many context switches.

clusters.title: Preemptive vs non-preemptive circumstances
clusters.technique: Preemption happens when running->ready or waiting->ready; non-preemptive SJF never context-switches mid-burst.

clusters.title: Thread concepts and models
clusters.technique: Threads share code, data and files but have own stack and registers; user library creates threads; concurrency one-to-one > many-to-many > many-to-one.

clusters.title: Process model basics (states, queue, PCB, heap, cascading termination)
clusters.technique: Running can go to ready (timer), waiting (I/O); ready queue holds ready processes in memory; PCB holds state, registers, scheduling info (not code); heap = dynamic memory; cascading termination.

clusters.title: OS-specific scheduling (Windows, Linux)
clusters.technique: Windows 16 non-real-time priorities (and 16 real-time); Linux supports preemptive priority and time-sharing.

clusters.title: Counting semaphore value after P and V operations
clusters.technique: final = initial - (#P) + (#V).
clusters.what_changes: Which of the three quantities is unknown.

clusters.title: Mutual exclusion and critical-section statements
clusters.technique: Only one process in critical section; structure entry/critical/exit/remainder; spin lock = busy waiting; unaware processes still have mutual exclusion, starvation, deadlock problems but not coherence.

clusters.title: Maximum processes for deadlock freedom
clusters.technique: Deadlock-free if R >= n(m-1)+1, so n_max = floor((R-1)/(m-1)).

clusters.title: Banker's algorithm passage
clusters.technique: Banker avoids deadlock; needs Max, Allocation, Available matrices/vectors; grants only if the system stays in a safe state.

clusters.title: Symbol table
clusters.technique: Symbol table used for storage allocation, type checking, duplicate-error suppression; hash table gives fastest access.

clusters.title: Compiler phases order and roles
clusters.technique: Lexical -> syntax -> semantic -> intermediate code -> optimization -> code generation; syntax analysis checks grammar.

examiner_mindset: Numerical questions (scheduling, disk scheduling, page-fault counting, paging arithmetic, semaphore arithmetic) form roughly a third of the unit; small data sets, always solvable by hand.
Same data is reused: june2019_q41 and june2023_q78 share one SSTF queue, nov2021_q75 and july2018_q59 share a preemptive SJF set, dec2023_q80 and june2025_q30 are the same question.

Passage-based multi-question sets (nov2020 disk, nov2021 paging, june2023 LRU array, june2024 Banker, dec2024 scheduling, june2025 disk queue) give 5 questions each and are the main source of repetition.
Match-the-following questions mix terms across OS areas; the same standard pairings recur (RAID levels, Banker = resource allocation).
Trap options: C-SCAN/SCAN differences (jump counted or not), the difference between FIFO and LRU for Belady, 'current needs' column in Banker.
Distractors are near-values from off-by-one or unit mistakes (KB vs bytes, ms vs seconds).
Difficulty is mostly easy to moderate; heavy theory such as formal proofs or code is never asked, but fork-counting appears occasionally.
Cross-unit overlap: Unit 5 questions on OS appear in matching with data structures and networking cloud terms; compiler and assembler items are minor.
Process management and file systems/disk scheduling alone take over 40% of the unit.
Never asked: kernel source code, detailed Windows internals beyond priority counts, deep distributed OS theory.

formulas.name: Deadlock-free process bound
formulas.formula: R >= n(m-1)+1, so n_max = floor((R-1)/(m-1))
formulas.note: R resources, each process needs m; e.g. R=12,m=4 gives 3

formulas.name: Banker: Need
formulas.formula: Need = Max - Allocation; safe if some order lets every process finish with Available
formulas.note: In dec2019_q28 'Current needs' column is actually the allocation

formulas.name: Disk capacity
formulas.formula: surfaces x tracks per surface x sectors per track x bytes per sector

formulas.name: Sector-address bits
formulas.formula: log2(surfaces x tracks x sectors)

formulas.name: Rotational delay
formulas.formula: max = 60/rpm seconds; average = half of that

formulas.name: Data transfer rate
formulas.formula: bytes per track x revolutions per second

formulas.name: Seek time
formulas.formula: total head movement x time per cylinder
formulas.note: SSTF picks nearest pending request each time

formulas.name: Disk policies
formulas.formula: SCAN goes to end then reverses; C-SCAN goes to end then jumps to start; LOOK/C-LOOK turn at the last request
formulas.note: C-SCAN return jump counted in textbook answers

formulas.name: Inode maximum file size
formulas.formula: (direct + p + p^2) x block size, p = block size/address size

formulas.name: Tape write time
formulas.formula: (data / recording density) / speed (+ inter-block gaps)

formulas.name: Paging sizes
formulas.formula: pages = VA/page size; offset bits = log2(page); frames = PM/page; page table size = pages x entry size

formulas.name: Internal fragmentation
formulas.formula: unused space in last page = pages x page size - process size
formulas.note: 34 KB with 4 KB pages gives 2 KB

formulas.name: EMAT with TLB
formulas.note: Single level page table; two-level adds extra m

formulas.name: EAT with page faults
formulas.formula: (1-p)m + p x fault time; or p + q/100 if one fault per 100

formulas.name: Swap time
formulas.formula: 2 x (size/transfer rate) + latencies

formulas.name: Belady's anomaly
formulas.formula: Occurs for FIFO; LRU and optimal are stack algorithms and have no anomaly

formulas.name: Little's law
formulas.formula: n = lambda x W

formulas.name: Scheduling times
formulas.formula: TAT = CT - AT; WT = TAT - BT; RT = first run - AT; HRRN ratio = (W+S)/S

formulas.name: RR worst-case wait
formulas.formula: (n-1) x q

formulas.name: Counting semaphore
formulas.formula: final = initial - #P + #V

formulas.name: fork count
formulas.formula: k sequential forks create 2^k processes
formulas.note: Count prints by tracing each fork

formulas.name: RAID levels
formulas.formula: 0 striping,1 mirror,2 bit ECC,3 bit parity,4 block parity,5 distributed block parity,6 P+Q

formulas.name: Linux interrupt priority
formulas.formula: user < kernel system service < bottom half < top half

formulas.name: Thread sharing
formulas.formula: Shared: code,data,files,address space. Private: stack,registers,PC
formulas.note: Threads of same process share address space

formulas.name: Thread model concurrency
formulas.formula: one-to-one > many-to-many > many-to-one
formulas.note: Many-to-one blocks entirely on a blocking call

formulas.name: Boot order
formulas.formula: ROM firmware -> boot block -> bootstrap loader -> kernel

formulas.name: Layered file system
formulas.formula: Application -> logical FS -> file organization module -> basic FS -> I/O control

formulas.name: File allocation
formulas.formula: Contiguous has external fragmentation; linked and indexed do not

formulas.name: Compiler phase order
formulas.formula: lexical, syntax, semantic, intermediate code, optimization, code generation
formulas.note: Hash table best for symbol table

formulas.formula: fork creates child; exec loads program; kill signals; clone selective sharing; wc -l; lpr; /etc/passwd; chmod -R a+x

clusters.title: Agile: which models/principles are agile
clusters.technique: Agile = XP, Scrum, FDD, ASD, Crystal, DSDM; NOT waterfall/spiral/incremental. Agile principles favour change, customer collaboration, working software, delivering increments; 'following the plan' is the anti-principle.
clusters.what_changes: Pick-the-agile-models, odd-one-out principle, or correct handling of unpredictability
clusters.skip_note: All three test 'agile = embrace change, incremental delivery'; one pass covers all.

clusters.title: Agile/FDD sequence and artifact matching
clusters.technique: Memorise FDD order: overall model, feature list, plan by feature, design by feature, build by feature. Agile flow: plan, design, develop, test, release. Scrum=sprint backlog, XP=CRC cards, ASD=speculate-collaborate-learn.
clusters.what_changes: Ordering vs matching of agile phases/artifacts
clusters.skip_note: Same memorised sequences/artifacts reappear; learn the lists once.

clusters.title: Cleanroom software engineering
clusters.technique: Cleanroom: incremental model, formal specification, statistical (usage-based) testing and certification, correctness verification (static); no unit testing/dynamic verification by developers.
clusters.what_changes: Which statement is false / which is not a strategy
clusters.skip_note: Same 3-4 facts about cleanroom each time.

clusters.title: Process model suitability matching
clusters.technique: Waterfall=stable requirements; incremental=core product quickly; evolutionary/prototype=unclear reqs; component-based=reuse, compromises inevitable; spiral=risk driven.
clusters.skip_note: Both are the same model-to-situation table.

clusters.title: Spiral model characteristics
clusters.technique: Spiral = risk-driven, evolutionary/cyclic, suited to changing/unclear requirements, large projects.

clusters.title: Prototype model phase order
clusters.technique: Order: requirements/quick play -> quick design -> build prototype -> customer evaluation -> refine -> deliver/engineer final product.
clusters.what_changes: Wording of steps differs, order same

clusters.title: SRS quality attribute definitions
clusters.technique: Map definition to attribute: unambiguous=one interpretation, consistent=no conflicts, verifiable=cost-effective check, complete, modifiable, traceable, ranked. Reliability is not an SRS attribute.
clusters.what_changes: Which attribute / which is NOT an attribute
clusters.skip_note: Same attribute list, different definition asked.

clusters.title: Elicitation and validation techniques
clusters.technique: Elicitation: interviews, questionnaires, ethnography (observation), prototyping, use cases/scenarios, JAD; DFD is analysis, not elicitation. Inspection/reviews/prototype/test-case generation validate requirements.

clusters.title: Cohesion types and ranking

clusters.title: Coupling types

examiner_mindset: Roughly 40% of questions are pure recall of definitions/lists; the rest are matching, ordering and true/false statement formats.

Topic tags are fuzzy: the same theme (maintenance, reengineering, V&V) is tagged under several topics, so study by theme.

units.name: Data Structures and Algorithms

topics.why: 32 questions (23%) present in 14 of 15 papers at about 2 per paper, steady across the period. The largest block: heaps, BST/AVL/B-tree, tree counting formulas, traversals.
what_to_study: Tree counting identities (m-ary: L=(m-1)I+1; strict binary: 2L-1 nodes; Catalan for count of binary trees)
Build/insert heaps by hand; build-heap O(n); min in max heap O(n)
AVL rotation types LL RR LR RL and counting rotations; AVL vs red-black trade-offs
B-tree: height bound, node size, insertion splits
Heap vs balanced BST for the right operations

topics.why: 25 questions (18%), present in 14 of 15 papers, 12 of them in the last 6 papers. The single biggest recurring block: master theorem, substitution, asymptotic ordering, complexity matching.
what_to_study: Master theorem all 3 cases with log/sqrt f(n); non-standard shapes T(3n/4)+1, T(2n/3)+1
Substitution n -> 2^m for T(sqrt n) recurrences
Order functions by growth (compare logs; n^log n vs 2^n vs n^1.5)
Asymptotic notation properties: O,Omega,o,omega transitivity and the worst/best-case definition
Memorise complexity tables: sorts, searches, graph algorithms, FFT, Fibonacci methods, A*/DFS/hill climbing space/time

topics.why: 21 questions (15%) in 11 of 15 papers; Dec 2022 passage (5 Qs) and June 2025 (4 Qs) show it is alive. Mix of conceptual matching and small numerical DP/greedy problems.
what_to_study: Greedy vs DP vs D&C vs backtracking: classify standard problems (Dijkstra, Kruskal, Huffman, fractional knapsack = greedy; Bellman-Ford, LCS, edit distance, OBST, 0/1 knapsack = DP; merge/quick/binary search, Strassen, closest pair, FFT = D&C; 8-queens = backtracking)
Fractional knapsack: sort by profit/weight, fill, take fraction of last item; O(n log n)
LCS table computation and subsequence reading
Huffman construction (merge two smallest repeatedly), average code length, weighted path length
DP development steps in order: characterize, define recursively, compute bottom-up, construct solution
FFT: polynomial multiplication in O(n lg n)

topics.topic: Graph Algorithms (BFS, DFS, MST, Shortest Path)
topics.why: 22 questions (16%) in 11 papers, but only 2 came in the last 6 papers (2023-2025) versus 20 in the first 9, so it is fading; kept High (not Must) because of the large historical share and two direct hits in Dec 2024 and June 2024 Re-Exam.
what_to_study: Run Prim and Kruskal by hand; MST weight; valid edge orders
DFS/BFS validity of traversal sequences (each next vertex must be a neighbour of the stack top / queue frontier)
Match algorithm to purpose and complexity (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, Prim, Kruskal, toposort, Edmonds-Karp)
DFS: no cross edges in undirected graph; applications are toposort and SCC
Flow network skew symmetry/conservation, Ford-Fulkerson O(E*f)

topics.why: 10 questions (7%) in 8 of 15 papers (53%), steady 1-2 per paper. Two near-identical linear probing questions appear in different years.
what_to_study: Simulate linear probing and closed hashing tables step by step
Chaining / linear / quadratic / double hashing definitions
Universal hashing: table size n^2 gives collision probability < 1/2

topics.why: 9 questions (6%) in 6 papers, but 7 of the 9 came in the last 6 papers (2023-2025), so it is rising. All are conceptual/definition level.
what_to_study: Queue variants and applications (circular, priority, deque, simple) and BFS-queue / DFS-stack
Circular queue empty/full conditions (one slot sacrificed)
XOR linked list, deque via two stacks, deleting a node when only a pointer to it is given
Sparse matrix types (lower triangular) and adjacency-matrix = sequential representation

topics.why: 8 questions (6%) in 7 papers; statement-type, mostly one per paper and concept-only.
what_to_study: If any NP-complete problem is in P then P=NP; NP-complete = NP and NP-hard
SAT, CIRCUIT-SAT, TSP decision, Hamiltonian cycle are NP-complete
co-NP: P subset of co-NP; NP != co-NP implies P != NP
Approximation: vertex cover 2-approx; TSP with triangle inequality 2-approx

what_to_study: Infix to postfix with precedence (^ right-assoc, then * /, then + -) and parentheses
Postfix and prefix evaluation with a stack (prefix: scan right to left)
Properties: operand order identical in infix/prefix/postfix; prefix is NOT reverse of postfix in general

In place: insertion, heap, quick (merge is not)
Radix/counting: linear time for range n^c; radix cost = digits x n x radix
