clusters.title: Fractional knapsack passage (Dec 2022)
clusters.technique: Compute p/w ratios, sort descending, fill greedily, take a fraction of the last item that does not fit. Greedy is optimal for fractional, not for 0/1.
clusters.what_changes: Capacity (15 vs 25), time complexity O(n log n) with n items, technique name, 0/1 vs fractional statement
clusters.skip_note: All five share one item table; solving cap 25 fully (48.1) also gives cap 15 (40) and the greedy/O(n log n) facts.

clusters.title: Longest common subsequence
clusters.technique: Fill LCS table: match -> diag+1 else max(up,left); read the sequence by backtracking.
clusters.what_changes: Sequences and whether length or the actual subsequence is asked
clusters.skip_note: Same LCS recurrence; length 4 both times.

clusters.title: Huffman coding computations and steps
clusters.technique: Repeatedly merge the two smallest weights; average length = sum(p*depth); weighted path length = sum of internal merge costs. Steps: leaves, priority queue, combine lowest, repeat.
clusters.what_changes: Probabilities vs integer weights vs step ordering
clusters.skip_note: One Huffman run + the step order covers all three.

clusters.title: DP development steps and properties
clusters.technique: Order: characterize optimal structure, recursive definition, compute bottom-up, construct solution. Only optimal-substructure is shared with greedy. Cyclic dependency breaks DP.
clusters.what_changes: Asked as ordering, common-steps, or true/false statements
clusters.skip_note: Same four-step template; know the order once.

clusters.title: Classify problems by design paradigm
clusters.technique: Memorise the paradigm table: greedy (Dijkstra, Kruskal, Prim, Huffman, fractional knapsack), DP (Bellman-Ford, LCS, edit distance, OBST, 0/1 knapsack, Floyd), D&C (merge, quick, binary search, Strassen, closest pair), backtracking (8-queens).
clusters.skip_note: Same table in every question; the matching rep covers all.

clusters.title: FFT polynomial multiplication / FFT complexities
clusters.technique: FFT evaluates and interpolates in O(n lg n); pointwise product O(n); so multiplying degree-n polynomials is theta(n lg n).
clusters.what_changes: Wording; June 2023 asks a match of FFT-related times
clusters.skip_note: Dec 2019 and Dec 2022 are exact repeats (n lg n).

clusters.title: Queue/stack variants and applications
clusters.technique: Know applications: circular queue-CPU scheduling, priority queue-Dijkstra, deque-palindrome check, queue-print, BFS-queue, DFS-stack, prefix-LISP, infix-syntax tree.
clusters.what_changes: Matching form vs single-answer deque property
clusters.skip_note: Same fact set re-asked as matching.

clusters.title: Asymptotic growth ordering
clusters.technique: Take logs or substitute big n; known chain: log n < sqrt n < n < n log n < n^1.5 < n^2 < n^log n < 2^n < n!.
clusters.what_changes: Functions, polynomial degrees, recurrences or search/sort names being ordered
clusters.skip_note: Same skill; one fully worked ordering plus the chain covers all.

clusters.title: Asymptotic notation properties
clusters.technique: Check definitions: O,Omega transitive; o,omega transitive; algorithm O(g) iff worst O(g); f=O(g) implies g=Omega(f).

clusters.title: Match algorithms to running times (sort/search/DP/AI)
clusters.technique: Recall table: insertion best O(n), binary search O(lg n), quick avg n lg n worst n^2, heap n lg n, Rabin-Karp theta((n-m+1)m), Fibonacci naive exponential, memoised O(n), matrix-power O(lg n), hill climbing O(1), DFS O(bm), A*/BFS O(b^d), D&C recurrences.
clusters.skip_note: Each is a table lookup; learn the table once.

clusters.title: Master theorem and simple recurrences
clusters.technique: Compare f(n) with n^(log_b a): smaller -> n^log_b a; equal -> times log n; larger -> f(n). For T(n)=T(cn)+1 get log n.
clusters.skip_note: All use the same three-case check.

clusters.title: Recurrences with sqrt(n) (substitution n=2^m)
clusters.technique: Set m = lg n, S(m)=T(2^m); T(n)=aT(sqrt n)+f becomes S(m)=aS(m/2)+f(m), then master theorem.
clusters.skip_note: Same substitution trick; one worked case suffices.

clusters.title: Infix to postfix conversion
clusters.technique: Stack of operators: pop while top has >= precedence (not for right-assoc ^); parentheses group; operands emitted immediately.
clusters.what_changes: Expression and whether options reorder operators; Dec 2022 Shift II asks properties

clusters.title: Postfix/prefix evaluation
clusters.technique: Postfix: left to right, push operands, apply on two pops (second pop is left operand). Prefix: right to left.
clusters.what_changes: Expression; final value, stack state, or ordering several values

clusters.title: Is this sequence a valid DFS?
clusters.topic: Graph Algorithms (BFS, DFS, MST, Shortest Path)
clusters.technique: Walk the sequence: each next vertex must be adjacent to a vertex still on the DFS stack path (go back only when stuck).

clusters.title: MST by hand (Prim/Kruskal)
clusters.topic: Graph Algorithms (BFS, DFS, MST, Shortest Path)
clusters.technique: Kruskal: sort edges, add if no cycle. Prim: grow from start picking min edge to new vertex. MST weight is same.
clusters.what_changes: Graph; asks weight, order, or invalid order
clusters.skip_note: Same hand simulation; do one Kruskal and one Prim.

clusters.title: Match graph algorithms to time complexities
clusters.topic: Graph Algorithms (BFS, DFS, MST, Shortest Path)
clusters.technique: Dijkstra O(V^2) (array) / O(E lg V) (heap); Prim O(E lg V); Kruskal O(E lg E); Bellman-Ford O(VE); Floyd-Warshall theta(V^3); toposort theta(V+E); Edmonds-Karp O(VE^2).
clusters.what_changes: Which subset of algorithms; notation O vs theta
clusters.skip_note: Same table; July 2018 asks the SSSP identity only.

clusters.title: Graph algorithm purpose and properties
clusters.topic: Graph Algorithms (BFS, DFS, MST, Shortest Path)
clusters.technique: Dijkstra: non-negative weights, single-source; Bellman-Ford: negative edges; Floyd/Warshall: all pairs/path matrix; Prim/Kruskal: MST. Shortest path need not have fewest edges.

clusters.title: BFS/DFS properties and applications
clusters.topic: Graph Algorithms (BFS, DFS, MST, Shortest Path)
clusters.technique: DFS: toposort, SCC; no cross edges in undirected DFS tree; BFS tree edges can join same level. Prim/Dijkstra are best-first, not BFS.

clusters.title: Max-flow facts
clusters.topic: Graph Algorithms (BFS, DFS, MST, Shortest Path)
clusters.technique: Flow: skew symmetry f(u,v)=-f(v,u) and conservation sum_v f(u,v)=0; Ford-Fulkerson O(E*f) for integer capacities.

clusters.title: Linear probing: location of key 18 (exact repeat)
clusters.technique: Insert in order with h=key mod 7, move to next free slot on collision; 18 lands at index 5.

clusters.title: Hash insertion simulation
clusters.technique: Compute h(x) for each key and probe forward to the next empty slot.
clusters.what_changes: Hash function and keys; asks table state or index
clusters.skip_note: Same simulation; july2018_q70 and june2023_q44 differ only in the hash function.

clusters.title: Collision resolution definitions
clusters.technique: Chaining=linked list; linear=next slot; quadratic=skip by squares; double=second hash; hash table backed by array.

clusters.title: NP-class statements
clusters.technique: Use: NPC subset of NP and NP-hard; one NPC in P implies P=NP; SAT/CIRCUIT-SAT/Hamiltonian/TSP-decision are NPC; P subset of co-NP.

clusters.title: Stability and in-place properties of sorts
clusters.technique: Stable: bubble, insertion, merge. In-place: insertion, heap, quick.

clusters.title: Linear-time and radix sorting
clusters.technique: Radix sort on d-digit numbers: O(d(n+k)); range n^2 -> two passes base n -> O(n). Count-based answer: items x digits x radix.

clusters.title: Build heap / insert into heap by hand
clusters.technique: Max-heapify from n/2 down (build) or sift-up on each insertion; write array.

clusters.title: Heap and priority-queue operation costs
clusters.technique: Build-heap O(n); heapify/insert/extract O(lg n); min in max-heap O(n); unsorted-array PQ insert O(1), extract-min O(n); heap cannot do dedup in O(lg n).

clusters.title: Tree counting identities
clusters.technique: m-ary full: L=(m-1)I+1; strict binary: n=2L-1; degree sum: L=1+sum (d-1)*n_d; leaves of complete binary tree = i+1.

clusters.title: Balanced tree concepts (AVL, RB, B, 2-3-4)
clusters.technique: AVL: strict balance, more rotations; RB: longest path <= 2x shortest, O(lg n); 2-3-4 tree equivalent to red-black; B-tree for disk; AVL rotations LL RR LR RL.
clusters.skip_note: Mostly definitions; dec2024_q81 reviews all properties.

clusters.title: B-tree computations
clusters.technique: Height h <= log_t((n+1)/2); node size = keys*key size + pointers*size; insertion worst case splits every level (+1 new root).

clusters.title: Tree traversals
clusters.technique: Inorder L-Root-R; reconstruct from preorder+inorder (root first from preorder, split inorder).
clusters.what_changes: Figure vs reconstruction vs ordering steps

clusters.title: BST build and measure
clusters.technique: Insert keys in order, then count left-subtree nodes or measure height (edges).

examiner_mindset: Dominant format is "match List I with List II" and "arrange in order": same fact tables (complexities, paradigms, applications) re-asked with shuffled options.
Easy conceptual definitions are ~half the unit; hand-simulations (probing, heap build, Kruskal/Prim, postfix) form the numerical half and are always small.

Reuse is heavy: the Dec 2018 / Nov 2021 / July 2018 linear-probing "key 18" question appears twice verbatim; the Dec 2019 and Dec 2022 FFT n lg n question repeats; infix-to-postfix appears nearly every year.
Complexity block rising: master theorem variants (2T(n/4)+sqrt n, 3T(n/4)+n lg n, T(3m/4)+1, T(2n/3)+1) and sqrt(n) substitutions are favourite non-trivial items.
Graph questions faded sharply after 2022 (2 in last six papers vs 20 earlier) while arrays/queues concept questions rose (7 vs 2).
Distractors: swapping Omega/O, theta vs O, n lg n vs n^2 for sorts, n^lg n vs 2^n, rotating match options by one position, "prefix is reverse of postfix".
Multi-question passages appear (Dec 2022 knapsack, 5 Qs): one table gives 5 marks.
Trap statements: Bellman-Ford labelled greedy (it is DP), heap sort labelled D&C (it is not), TSP-tour called 3-approx (it is 2), EXP written 2^k.
Cross-unit overlap: DFS/BFS stack-queue (Unit 3-style programming), AI search complexities (hill climbing, A*), Dijkstra/Prim in networks-style matching.
He never asks long proofs, amortised analysis, red-black insertion step traces, Johnson/KMP algorithm traces or NP-reduction construction; all questions are 1-2 minute solvable.

formulas.name: Master theorem
formulas.formula: T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n): f<n^log_b a -> theta(n^log_b a); f=n^log_b a -> theta(f lg n); f>n^log_b a (regularity) -> theta(f)
formulas.note: 2T(n/4)+sqrt n -> sqrt n lg n (equal case); 3T(n/4)+n lg n -> n lg n (case 3).

formulas.name: Constant-work shrink
formulas.formula: T(n)=T(cn)+1 -> theta(lg n) for 0<c<1
formulas.note: T(3m/4)+1 and T(2n/3)+1 are both lg.

formulas.name: sqrt recurrence
formulas.formula: T(n)=aT(sqrt n)+f(lg n): let m=lg n -> S(m)=aS(m/2)+f(m)
formulas.note: 2T(sqrt n)+lg n -> O(lg n lg lg n); 4T(sqrt n)+lg^2 n -> theta(lg^2 n lg lg n).

formulas.name: Growth chain
formulas.formula: lg n < sqrt n < n < n lg n < n^1.5 < n^2 < n^lg n < 2^n < n!
formulas.note: n^lg n is superpolynomial but below 2^n.

formulas.name: Worst/best-case O
formulas.formula: Algorithm is O(g) iff worst case O(g); f=O(g) <=> g=Omega(f); little-o and little-omega transitive
formulas.note: O and o are not interchangeable; f=O(g) does not give omega.

formulas.name: Sort/search complexities
formulas.formula: binary search lg n; insertion best n worst n^2; merge n lg n; quick avg n lg n worst n^2; heap n lg n; selection n^2

formulas.name: Graph algorithm complexities
formulas.formula: Dijkstra V^2 (heap E lg V); Prim E lg V; Kruskal E lg E; Bellman-Ford VE; Floyd-Warshall V^3; toposort/BFS/DFS V+E; Edmonds-Karp VE^2; Ford-Fulkerson E*f
formulas.note: Kruskal sometimes written O(E lg V) - same.

formulas.name: Edge relaxation
formulas.formula: d[v] = min(d[v], d[u]+w(u,v))

formulas.name: Fractional knapsack
formulas.formula: Sort by p/w descending; take whole items then fraction of next; time O(n lg n)
formulas.note: 0/1 knapsack needs DP; fractional is greedy.

formulas.name: LCS recurrence
formulas.formula: c[i,j]=c[i-1,j-1]+1 if x_i=y_j else max(c[i-1,j],c[i,j-1])

formulas.name: Huffman
formulas.formula: Merge two least weights repeatedly; average length = sum p_i*len_i; weighted path length = sum of all merged internal node weights

formulas.name: DP steps
formulas.formula: Characterize structure -> define recursively -> compute bottom-up -> construct solution
formulas.note: Only step 1 is shared with greedy.

formulas.name: FFT
formulas.formula: Multiply degree-n polynomials in theta(n lg n); point-value product theta(n); Horner evaluation at n points theta(n^2)

formulas.name: Full m-ary tree
formulas.formula: L=(m-1)*I+1; total nodes = m*I+1

formulas.name: Strict binary tree
formulas.formula: n = 2L-1 nodes; internal = L-1

formulas.name: Degree-sum leaves
formulas.formula: L = 1 + sum over internal nodes (degree-1)

formulas.name: Catalan number
formulas.formula: Binary trees with n nodes = C(2n,n)/(n+1)

formulas.name: Heap facts
formulas.formula: Build-heap theta(n); heapify O(lg n); nodes of height h <= ceil(n/2^(h+1)); min of max-heap lies in leaves O(n)

formulas.name: B-tree

clusters.title: CFL closure properties (union yes, intersection/complement no)
clusters.technique: Memorise the table: CFL closed under union, concatenation, star, reversal, homomorphism, intersection with regular; NOT under intersection, complement, difference. Counterexample is a^n b^n c^n = (a^n b^n c^m) ∩ (a^m b^n c^n).
clusters.what_changes: Which operations are asked; wording as true/false statements, two-statement format, or a concrete L1 ∩ L2 computation.
clusters.skip_note: All nine just test the same closure table; one pass of the table plus the a^n b^n c^n counterexample covers them.

clusters.title: Closure/regularity of regular-language operations (quotient, homomorphism, reversal, union with L*)
clusters.technique: Regular languages are closed under every standard operation; apply the operation to the DFA/regex (substitute symbols for homomorphism, reverse arrows for reversal). L ∪ A* = A* is regular.
clusters.what_changes: The operation (prefix-half quotient, homomorphism, reversal, union with Σ*).
clusters.skip_note: Answer is always "still regular"; the only skill is applying h to each symbol of the regex.

clusters.title: Language-class closure matching (complement/union/intersection of REC, RE, CF, regular)
clusters.technique: Use: REC closed under complement and union; RE closed under union but not complement; complement of CFL is only recursive (CSL); regular* ∩ CFL is CFL. Compose upward.
clusters.what_changes: Which combination of classes is matched; same three-row structure.
clusters.skip_note: Same three row pattern, only the pairing order changes.

clusters.title: Chomsky hierarchy: types, automata, production forms, containment
clusters.technique: Type3=regular=FA, Type2=CFG=PDA, Type1=CSG=LBA, Type0=RE=TM. Regular ⊂ CFL ⊂ CSL ⊂ Recursive ⊂ RE. Type-3 is the only epsilon-free type by form.
clusters.what_changes: Matching tables (grammar-automaton, grammar-production form), ordering by power, containment chain.
clusters.skip_note: Same hierarchy table rephrased every time.

clusters.title: Classify a language with counting constraints (CF vs not CF vs CSL)
clusters.technique: One counter (a^n b^n, n_a+n_b=n_c, a^(n+m) b^n a^m) is CF; two independent equalities across three or more blocks (a^n b^n c^n, i=j=k) are not CF but CSL. Check by whether one stack can match all dependencies.
clusters.what_changes: The exact exponent relation among blocks.
clusters.skip_note: All ask "can a single stack do it"; learn the rule, not the instances.

clusters.title: CNF/GNF form and derivation-length facts
clusters.technique: CNF rules: A→BC or A→a. Derivation of a string of length n in CNF takes 2n-1 steps. Conversion bound (K-1)|P|+|T|. GNF: A→aα.
clusters.what_changes: Recall a formula vs identify which grammar is in CNF/GNF.
clusters.skip_note: CNF definition plus 2n-1 covers the family.

clusters.title: Ambiguity: identify ambiguous grammars, definition, dangling else
clusters.technique: Ambiguous iff some string has two parse trees (equivalently two leftmost or two rightmost derivations). Test the grammar with SS, SbS, or asbs patterns; if/else with unmatched else is ambiguous. Palindrome-like wwR is not inherently ambiguous; aⁿbⁿcᵐ ∪ aⁿbᵐcᵐ is.
clusters.what_changes: Which grammars are given; definition options.
clusters.skip_note: Find two trees for S→SS or SbS style grammars once and you can do every variant.

clusters.title: What language does this grammar generate / string property
clusters.technique: Expand productions symbolically, find the invariant (parity, ordering, lengths) and test short strings against options.
clusters.what_changes: Grammar and options; includes length-pattern matching for S→a^kSa^k|aa.
clusters.skip_note: All reduce to deriving a few short strings; do the recent one for the method.

clusters.title: Construct or compare grammars for a given language
clusters.technique: Test each option grammar on the shortest strings of the language (and a string that must be excluded). For equivalence, compare the sets generated by recursion (SS and λ closure).
clusters.what_changes: Target language: a^n b^(n-3), strings containing abb, concatenation of regex branches, equivalence of aSb|bSa|SS variants.
clusters.skip_note: Eliminate-by-counterexample; the same short-string test works for all.

clusters.title: PDA language from transitions
clusters.technique: Trace stack effect: pushes per a, pops per b gives ratio language (push 3 pop 1 gives a^n b^3n; 11 per a gives a^2n b^n). Start-state epsilon move to final adds the empty string (n≥0 vs n>0).
clusters.what_changes: Push amount and pop count; n≥0 vs n>0.
clusters.skip_note: Same trace; ratios and the n≥0/n>0 boundary are the only changes.

clusters.title: Automata power facts (PDA, multi-stack, grammar types recognised)
clusters.technique: PDA recognises CFL (and regular); two stacks = TM; DPDA with prefix property corresponds to LR(0).

clusters.title: CFG simplification and decision on CFL (reduced grammar, order, finiteness)
clusters.technique: Order: remove epsilon, then unit, then useless (non-generating before unreachable). Finiteness of CFL decided on non-redundant CNF grammar of L-{Λ} by looking for a cycle.
clusters.what_changes: Compute reduced grammar vs recall order vs decision algorithm.
clusters.skip_note: Do the reduced grammar example once.

clusters.title: Identify grammar type / form of productions
clusters.technique: Classify by LHS and RHS shape: single non-terminal LHS = CF; right-linear = regular; A→BC|a = CNF; LL(1) grammars parsable by recursive descent.

clusters.title: Dec 2024 passage: automata for strings containing abb
clusters.technique: Strings over {a,b} containing abb: DFA with 4 states, final state absorbing; regex (a+b)*abb(a+b)*; grammar S→AabbA, A→aA|bA|ε. Check option by testing abb, ab, aabb.
clusters.what_changes: Question asks for DFA, language form, regex, grammar or minimum-state identification.
clusters.skip_note: Whole passage is one machine seen five ways; build it once.

clusters.title: Membership of strings in L* for L={ab,aa,baa}
clusters.technique: Greedily parse into blocks ab, aa, baa; a string fails if some a-run leaves a dangling single a or b start that cannot be matched.

clusters.title: Count states/final states in (minimal) DFA
clusters.technique: Unary multiples of n: n states (the answer key shows n+1 for a particular form). Minimal DFA via table filling; merge states with equal outputs. Counts for n-state automata: initial 1, final 0..n.

clusters.title: Read an automaton: language, regex, equivalence
clusters.technique: Track parity/pattern state; for regex use state elimination or Arden R=Q+RP gives Q P*. Equivalence: minimise both and compare.
clusters.skip_note: All require describing what each state remembers.

clusters.title: NFA/DFA/epsilon-NFA conceptual facts and conversion
clusters.technique: NFA and DFA recognise the same class; epsilon-closure for shortest string; equivalent machines accept the same language; construction order: problem, regex, NFA-ε, DFA, min DFA.

clusters.title: Regex containment and equivalence
clusters.technique: Rewrite each regex as a description set; (a*+b)*=(a+b)*; s=aa*b ⊂ a*b; a(a+b)+ ⊂ a(a+b)*. Check inclusion by sample strings.

clusters.title: Regex algebra and writing a regex for a language
clusters.technique: φ+L=L, εL=L, φL=φ; precedence star > concatenation > union. For a^n b^m with bounds, write a^4 a* (λ+b+bb+bbb).

clusters.title: Pumping lemma statements and non-regular languages
clusters.technique: Regular PL: |xy|≤p, |y|≥1. CFL PL: |vx|≥1, |vwx|≤p. Languages needing unbounded comparison (n≠k, a^(n+k) with ordering, square lengths, ww) are not regular; a^(n^2) is not regular too.
clusters.what_changes: Which language or which PL parameter.
clusters.skip_note: One PL statement plus unbounded-count rule.

clusters.title: Parser power ordering and parser types
clusters.technique: LR(0) < SLR < LALR < CLR(1); LL(1) and recursive descent are top-down; LR family bottom-up; Yacc generates LALR(1); operator precedence is weakest bottom-up.

clusters.title: Shift-reduce parser basics (derivation, scan order, conflicts, stack configuration)
clusters.technique: Bottom-up = rightmost derivation in reverse, scans left to right, uses stack, input buffer, table; conflicts resolved by precedence/associativity.

clusters.title: LR items, handles and GOTO
clusters.technique: A→ε yields item A→·; GOTO(I,X) moves dot over X then closure; handle is the leftmost simple phrase reduced at each step.

clusters.title: LL(1)/FOLLOW computation
clusters.technique: FOLLOW(X) = FIRST of what comes after X; if nullable add FOLLOW of the parent. LL(1) requires unambiguous grammar with no left recursion and disjoint FIRST.

clusters.title: Compiler phases and their roles
clusters.technique: Order: lexical, syntax, semantic, intermediate code, optimisation, code generation. Semantic analysis does type checking/conversion; symbol table holds identifiers and attributes.

clusters.title: Intermediate code, SDT and syntax-tree uses
clusters.technique: Forms: syntax tree, DAG, postfix, three-address code (quadruples, triples, indirect triples). SDT used for type checking, syntax tree, TAC; quads count = operators.
clusters.skip_note: Concept recall plus one operator count.

clusters.title: Code optimisation concepts
clusters.technique: Constant folding = compile-time evaluation; loops identified by dominators, depth-first order, reducible graphs.

clusters.title: June 2025 TAC passage: leaders, flow graph, dominators, optimisation
clusters.technique: Leaders: first instruction, targets of jumps, instruction after a jump. Build blocks leader to leader, draw edges, derive dominators.
clusters.skip_note: One TAC listing used five times.

clusters.title: Decidability: Rice theorem and TM undecidable problems
clusters.technique: Any non-trivial property of L(M) is undecidable (equivalence, emptiness, finiteness, regularity). Halting is undecidable. Properties of the machine code itself or bounded simulation are decidable.

clusters.title: Decidability per language class
clusters.technique: Regular: all decidable. CFL: membership/emptiness/finiteness decidable, equivalence/universality undecidable. CSL: membership decidable, emptiness undecidable. Recursive: membership decidable, emptiness undecidable.

clusters.title: Post correspondence problem instances
clusters.technique: Look for a sequence where concatenations from both lists match; check length balance and first/last symbols. PCP in general is undecidable.

clusters.title: TM design passage a^n b^m c^n d^m transitions
clusters.technique: Mark one a with X1 then move right to matching c, mark with X2; error entries are transitions that move into a wrong symbol class. Track which mark each state seeks.
clusters.what_changes: Each question picks a different state/symbol cell.

clusters.title: TM basics: definition, transition function, language from δ
clusters.technique: Single-tape δ: Q×Γ→Q×Γ×{L,R}; multi-tape adds k tapes and S. Recursive = halts on all inputs. TM exists for every regular and CF language. aⁿbⁿ marking machine includes n≥1.

formulas.name: Chomsky hierarchy
formulas.formula: Regular ⊂ DCFL ⊂ CFL ⊂ CSL ⊂ Recursive ⊂ RE; Type3=FA, Type2=PDA, Type1=LBA, Type0=TM
formulas.note: Recursive sits between CSL and RE.

formulas.name: CFL closure
formulas.formula: Closed: ∪, ·, *, reversal, homomorphism, ∩ regular. Not closed: ∩, complement, difference
formulas.note: CFL − regular is CF; CFL ∩ CFL is not.

formulas.name: Regular closure
formulas.formula: Closed under all of union, concat, star, complement, intersection, reversal, homomorphism, quotient

formulas.name: Class closure
formulas.formula: REC closed under complement; RE not closed under complement; regular* ∩ CFL is CFL

formulas.name: CNF form
formulas.formula: A → BC or A → a; derivation of length-n string takes 2n-1 steps
formulas.note: Count n-1 binary + n terminal rules.

formulas.name: CNF conversion bound
formulas.note: Per answer key of this question.

formulas.name: GNF
formulas.formula: A → a α (terminal first then variables)

formulas.name: Ambiguity
formulas.formula: Ambiguous iff some string has ≥2 parse trees ⇔ ≥2 leftmost derivations ⇔ ≥2 rightmost
formulas.note: More than one derivation alone is not ambiguity.

formulas.name: Pumping lemma (regular)
formulas.formula: w=xyz, |xy|≤p, |y|≥1, xy^i z ∈ L for all i≥0

formulas.name: Pumping lemma (CFL)
formulas.formula: w=uvwxy, |vwx|≤p, |vx|≥1, uv^i wx^i y ∈ L

formulas.name: Regex identities
formulas.formula: φ+L=L; εL=L; φL=φ; (a*+b)*=(a+b)*; precedence star > concat > union

formulas.name: Arden theorem
formulas.formula: R = Q + RP ⇒ R = QP*

formulas.name: Moore/Mealy
formulas.formula: Every Moore machine has an equivalent Mealy machine and vice versa

formulas.name: PDA power
formulas.formula: PDA = CFL; two stacks = TM; DPDA+prefix property ↔ LR(0)
formulas.note: One stack is not enough for a^n b^n c^n.

formulas.name: Decidability table
formulas.formula: Regular: all decidable. CFL: membership, emptiness, finiteness decidable; equivalence, universality undecidable. CSL: membership decidable, emptiness undecidable. Recursive: membership decidable, emptiness undecidable
formulas.note: Common trap: CSL membership is decidable.

formulas.name: Rice theorem
formulas.formula: Every non-trivial semantic property of L(M) is undecidable
formulas.note: Properties of M itself (e.g., bounded cells) can be decidable.

formulas.name: PCP
formulas.formula: Undecidable in general; solve instances by matching strings

formulas.name: TM definitions
formulas.formula: δ: Q×Γ→Q×Γ×{L,R}; multi-tape δ: Q×Γ^k→Q×Γ^k×{L,R,S}^k; recursive language = TM halts on all inputs
formulas.note: Recursive requires halting on rejected strings too.

formulas.name: Parser power
formulas.formula: LR(0) < SLR < LALR(1) < CLR(1); LL(1) ⊂ LR(1); Yacc = LALR
formulas.note: LALR is weaker than CLR, stronger than SLR.

formulas.name: Bottom-up parsing
formulas.formula: Reverse of rightmost derivation; scans left to right; stack+buffer+table

formulas.name: FOLLOW
formulas.formula: FOLLOW(X) ⊇ FIRST(β) for A→αXβ; if β nullable add FOLLOW(A)
formulas.note: ε never in FOLLOW; $ for start symbol.

formulas.name: LR item
formulas.formula: A → ε yields item A → ·

formulas.name: Quadruple count
formulas.formula: One quadruple per operator

formulas.name: Basic block leaders
formulas.formula: First instruction; target of any jump; instruction immediately after a jump
formulas.note: Middle instruction is not a leader.

formulas.name: Compiler phases order
formulas.formula: Lexical → syntax → semantic → intermediate code → optimisation → code generation

formulas.name: Constant folding
formulas.formula: Compile-time evaluation of constant expressions

formulas.name: L* membership
formulas.formula: Parse into {ab,aa,baa} blocks greedily

clusters.topic: Data Link Layer, Error Control & Flow Control
clusters.technique: Frame relay frame: Flag, Address, Information, FCS, Flag; frame relay detects errors but gives no ack/flow control; PPP gives framing, link setup, authentication but no flow control or sequence numbering; X.25 is connection-oriented with SVCs.
clusters.what_changes: Which protocol and which property is asked.
clusters.skip_note: All use the same short fact sheet on three WAN protocols.

clusters.title: Subnetting passage (130.56.0.0/16 into 1024 subnets)
clusters.technique: Subnet bits = log2(subnets); new prefix = old + bits; addresses per subnet = 2^(32-prefix); first = block base, last = base + size - 1; last subnet = top of the parent block.
clusters.what_changes: Quantity asked: addresses, prefix, mask, first/last of first or last subnet.
clusters.skip_note: Single worked passage; the same numbers answer all five.

clusters.title: IPv4 classes, ranges and special addresses
clusters.technique: Class first octets: A 0-127 (loopback 127), B 128-191, C 192-223, D 224-239, E 240-255. Class A is 1/2 of space, B 1/4, C 1/8 (12.5%).
clusters.what_changes: Asks last address, share of space, class of a given address, or loopback facts.
clusters.skip_note: Memorising the class table answers all of them.

clusters.title: Subnet mask and host/subnet counting
clusters.technique: Hosts per subnet = 2^(host bits) - 2; subnets = 2^(subnet bits) (minus 2 in old classful convention as in nov2021_q95); AND address with mask to compare networks.
clusters.what_changes: Mask value, class, required subnets or hosts.
clusters.skip_note: Same bit-counting recipe; do one class B mask problem and one same-network check.

clusters.title: CIDR block splitting and route aggregation
clusters.technique: Split a prefix by halves/quarters (add 1 bit or 2 bits); aggregate contiguous blocks by shortening the prefix.
clusters.skip_note: Both rely on prefix-length arithmetic on contiguous blocks.

clusters.title: IP fragmentation across a smaller MTU
clusters.technique: Data per fragment = MTU - 20 header, rounded to multiple of 8 (820 -> 800). 1400 data + 20 = 1420 -> fragments of 800 and 600 data; offset in 8-byte units; MF=1 except last; TCP header only in first fragment.
clusters.what_changes: Different statement asked (fragment count, offset, flags, ports) on same MTU 1500/820 scenario.

clusters.title: IPv4 header hex decoding
clusters.technique: Hex 45 00 0054 ...: first nibble version, second HLEN (x4 bytes), bytes 3-4 total length, byte 9 TTL, byte 10 protocol (06 TCP, 11 UDP, 01 ICMP); efficiency = (total - header)/total.
clusters.what_changes: Which field is asked from the same header.
clusters.skip_note: Same decoding map; one worked example covers all.

clusters.title: IP/TCP header field facts and order
clusters.technique: Fields: version, HLEN, service type, total length, identification, flags, fragment offset, TTL, protocol, checksum, addresses, options. TTL, checksum and fragment fields change in transit; addresses do not. Fragment offset is IP, not TCP.
clusters.what_changes: Ordering, which field changes, or odd one out.
clusters.skip_note: All draw on the same header layout.

clusters.title: Ethernet delay calculation (10 Mbps, 2500 m, 512 B)
clusters.technique: Tt = frame bits / rate; Tp = distance/speed.

clusters.title: CSMA/CD minimum frame size
clusters.technique: Min frame bits = bandwidth x 2Tp (round-trip); reverse to get speed/distance.
clusters.what_changes: Forward (find frame size) vs reverse (find signal speed).

clusters.title: MAC protocol classification and multiple-access facts
clusters.technique: Random access: ALOHA, CSMA (1-persistent, non-persistent, p-persistent), CSMA/CD wired, CSMA/CA wireless. Controlled: reservation, polling, token passing. Channelization: FDMA, TDMA, CDMA (orthogonal codes).
clusters.what_changes: Matching, true/false statement set, or select-the-examples.

clusters.title: Ethernet/MAC address facts
clusters.technique: 48-bit address in hex; LSB of first byte 0 = unicast, 1 = multicast, all F = broadcast; MAC is globally unique.
clusters.what_changes: Address type, binary-to-hex conversion, uniqueness scope.

clusters.title: RSA computation
clusters.technique: n = p*q; phi = (p-1)(q-1); e*d = 1 mod phi; C = M^e mod n.
clusters.what_changes: Given p,q and either e or d; asks other key and cipher value.

clusters.title: Classical ciphers (Caesar, transposition) and key exchange
clusters.technique: Caesar shifts each letter by k (decrypt = shift back k); transposition permutes positions; Diffie-Hellman exchanges secret keys.

clusters.title: Symmetric cipher block and key sizes
clusters.technique: DES 64-bit block, 56-bit key; 3DES 168; IDEA 64/128; Blowfish 64/32-448; AES 128 block, keys 128/192/256; RSA key about 1024+; RC4 is stream.
clusters.what_changes: Matching table or statement set; same size numbers.
clusters.skip_note: One table of block/key sizes answers all.

clusters.title: Firewall function and filtering criteria
clusters.technique: Firewall filters in/out traffic by source/destination IP, TCP/UDP ports; VPN simulates a private leased line.
clusters.what_changes: Which criteria or what primary function.

clusters.title: Public-key, hash and digital-signature concepts
clusters.technique: Encrypt with receiver public key for secrecy; sign by encrypting hash/digest with sender private key; hash gives fixed-length digest; AES symmetric, RSA asymmetric.

clusters.title: OSI layer function matching and ordering
clusters.technique: Physical: raw bits; Data link: frames, MAC, piggybacking; Network: routing, logical address, billing; Transport: end-to-end, segmentation; Session: dialog/token mgmt; Presentation: syntax; Application: user interface.
clusters.what_changes: Which functions/protocols are on the list (SLIP data link, BGP network, UDP transport, SNMP application).
clusters.skip_note: Same layer-function matrix; june2023_q22 and dec2022_q74 are identical.

clusters.title: Which layer does what (PDU names, encryption, segmentation)
clusters.technique: PDUs: frame (link), packet (network), segment (transport). IP is host-to-host, TCP process-to-process. Encryption is presentation/application. Session: dialog control, token management, synchronization.
clusters.skip_note: All answered from the same layer fact sheet.

clusters.title: Period to frequency conversion
clusters.technique: f = 1/T; T = 100 ms gives 10 Hz = 10^-2 kHz.

clusters.title: Throughput calculation
clusters.technique: Throughput = bits successfully delivered per second = (rate of requests x size in bits).

clusters.title: Nyquist and Shannon limits
clusters.technique: Nyquist bit rate = 2B log2(L); sampling rate >= 2 f_max; Shannon C = B log2(1 + SNR).

clusters.title: Circuit vs packet switching statements
clusters.technique: Circuit switching reserves resources at setup, constant delay; packet switching shares links, variable delay, no dedicated path.

clusters.title: Line coding schemes
clusters.technique: Average bandwidth: NRZ-L N/2, MLT-3 N/3, 2B1Q N/4, 4D-PAM5 N/8; Manchester is self-clocking with two signal elements per bit; NRZ, Manchester, AMI are encodings; Hamming code is not a line code.
clusters.what_changes: Matching vs statement vs odd one out.

clusters.title: TCP behaviour after server crash
clusters.technique: After reboot the server has no connection state; client data gets RST; client waiting without keepalive may hang.

clusters.title: UDP versus TCP services
clusters.technique: UDP is connectionless, offers no flow/congestion control or retransmission; TCP has both.
clusters.what_changes: Statements about which protocol does what.

clusters.title: Congestion control mechanisms
clusters.technique: Choke packet notifies source; token bucket burst time = capacity/(output rate - fill rate).
clusters.skip_note: Two small items; token bucket formula is the only calculation.

clusters.title: Wireless technology matching (CDMA, GSM, UMTS, WiFi)
clusters.technique: CDMA multiple access, GSM FDMA+TDMA hybrid, UMTS faster mobile data, WiFi wireless LAN.

clusters.title: Cloud service models and virtualization
clusters.technique: SaaS software stack; PaaS development environment; IaaS infrastructure; hypervisor then VMs then resources then workloads; Azure OS-like platform, CloudFront CDN.

clusters.title: Cellular generations
clusters.technique: AMPS 1G analog; IS-95 2G CDMA/DSSS; 3G broadband CDMA.

clusters.title: Sliding window mechanics (steps and Go-back-N variables)
clusters.topic: Data Link Layer, Error Control & Flow Control
clusters.technique: Sliding window: send window, ack, slide; in Go-back-N Sn stays at window end, only Sf moves on ack.

examiner_mindset: Format mix: heavy on matching (List I/List II), arrange-in-order and multi-statement combos; pure numeric questions are about 20-25 of 167 and are single-step substitutions.

Exact repeats are common: Dec 2022 Shift I and II share CRC, MTU fragmentation and Ethernet delay questions; June 2023 reuses the fragmentation and Ethernet delay problems; period-to-frequency appears in 2018 and 2020.
Passage sets (sliding window Sep 2022, subnetting Dec 2022 Shift II, IPv4 header June 2023) give 5 questions from one setup, so one worked example is worth 5 marks.
Standard numbers are reused: 10 Mbps, 512-byte frame, 2500 m, 2e8 m/s; MTU 1500/820, 1400-byte TCP segment; header 45 00 00 54; RSA p,q small (3,11; 13,5).
Security is the largest topic (26) but mostly recall: key and block sizes, hash and digital-signature roles, RSA arithmetic, firewall basics; no deep protocol analysis.

Distractors: options differ by one detail (ordering swapped, 2^n vs 2^n - 2, 1-persistent vs 2-persistent, SYN vs ACK number); some answer keys have inconsistent options (Ethernet delay, Dec 2022 Shift II q35 vs June 2023 q81), so follow the key.
Recent papers (2023-2025) emphasise IP header/fragmentation, wireless/cloud/MANET matching and ordering questions; classical ciphers and sliding-window calculations appeared mostly 2018-2022.
Cross-unit overlap: cloud, virtualization, IoT, social networks and MANET belong to the emerging-networks end of this unit; hash and RSA overlap with theory-of-computation style number arithmetic.
He never asks: routing algorithm computation beyond a single distance-vector update, OSPF/BGP internals, TCP congestion window plots, or full-length subnet design with VLSM.
Difficulty is low: about 70% of questions are difficulty 1-2 recall; the few hard ones are the sliding-window passage and the distance-vector update.

formulas.name: Transmission delay
formulas.formula: Tt = frame size (bits) / bandwidth (bps)

formulas.name: Propagation delay
formulas.formula: Tp = distance / propagation speed
formulas.note: Watch units: km vs m, us per km vs km/s.

formulas.name: Bandwidth-delay product
formulas.formula: BDP = bandwidth x delay (RTT if round trip given)

formulas.name: Optimal sliding-window size
formulas.formula: W = 1 + 2Tp/Tt

formulas.name: Sliding-window efficiency / throughput
formulas.formula: efficiency = W / (1 + 2Tp/Tt) capped at 1; throughput = efficiency x bandwidth

formulas.name: Error detection/correction distance
formulas.formula: Detect s errors: d_min = s + 1; correct t errors: d_min = 2t + 1
formulas.note: Mixing the two is the usual trap.

formulas.name: Hamming distance
formulas.formula: Number of bit positions where two words differ (weight of XOR)

formulas.name: CRC codeword
formulas.formula: Codeword = dataword || remainder (remainder from modulo-2 division after appending zeros)
formulas.note: (x+1) factor of G(x) catches all odd-bit errors (nov2021_q100).

formulas.name: Bit stuffing flag
formulas.formula: Frame flag 01111110 = 0x7E; stuff 0 after five consecutive 1s

formulas.name: Nyquist bit rate
formulas.formula: C = 2B log2(L)
formulas.note: Noiseless channel only; sampling rate >= 2 f_max.

formulas.name: Shannon capacity
formulas.formula: C = B log2(1 + SNR)
formulas.note: Noisy channel; SNR is a ratio, not dB.

formulas.name: Frequency and period
formulas.formula: f = 1/T

formulas.name: Fully connected links
formulas.note: Symmetric keys for N persons also N(N-1)/2 (dec2018_q90).

formulas.name: CSMA/CD minimum frame
formulas.formula: L_min = bandwidth x 2Tp

formulas.name: Slotted ALOHA throughput
formulas.formula: S = G e^(-G); pure ALOHA S = G e^(-2G)

formulas.name: Token bucket burst duration
formulas.formula: T = C / (M - rho) = capacity / (output rate - token rate)

formulas.name: Token ring 1-bit delay
formulas.formula: distance per bit = propagation speed / bit rate

formulas.name: Hosts per subnet
formulas.formula: 2^(host bits) - 2; subnets = 2^(subnet bits)
formulas.note: Subtract 2 for network and broadcast addresses.

formulas.name: Subnetting a block
formulas.formula: new prefix = old prefix + log2(subnets); addresses = 2^(32 - prefix)

formulas.name: IP fragmentation
formulas.formula: data per fragment = floor((MTU - 20)/8)*8; offset = bytes/8

formulas.name: IPv4 header decode
formulas.formula: byte0 low nibble HLEN x 4; bytes 2-3 total length; byte 8 TTL; byte 9 protocol (6 TCP, 17 UDP, 1 ICMP)

formulas.name: RSA
formulas.formula: n = pq; phi = (p-1)(q-1); ed = 1 mod phi; C = M^e mod n; M = C^d mod n

formulas.name: Symmetric key count
formulas.formula: N(N-1)/2 keys for N parties
formulas.note: Public-key needs only N key pairs.

formulas.name: Cipher sizes
formulas.formula: DES 64-bit block/56-bit key; 3DES 168; AES 128 block, 128/192/256 key; IDEA 64/128; Blowfish 32-448
formulas.note: DES has 16 rounds; function steps: expansion, XOR key, S-box, P-box.

formulas.name: Line coding average bandwidth
formulas.formula: NRZ-L N/2; MLT-3 N/3; 2B1Q N/4; 4D-PAM5 N/8; Manchester bit rate = half baud
formulas.note: Manchester needs twice the bandwidth of NRZ.

formulas.name: DHCP sequence
formulas.formula: Discover, Offer, Request, Ack

formulas.name: Hierarchical routing table size
formulas.formula: entries = routers in own region + other regions in cluster + other clusters

formulas.name: Piconet
formulas.formula: 1 master + up to 7 active slaves

what_to_study: Alpha-beta facts: same value, ordering, initial bounds

clusters.title: Dual pair of fuzzy t-norm and s-norm
clusters.technique: Use t(x,y)=1-s(1-x,1-y), so s(x,y)=1-t(1-x,1-y). Substitute 1-x,1-y into t, simplify 1 - (1-x)(1-y)/((1-x)+(1-y)-(1-x)(1-y)).
clusters.what_changes: Either recall the definition (june2019) or derive s for a given t (dec2019).
clusters.skip_note: Once you can derive s from t, the definition question is trivial.

clusters.title: Fuzzy set operations on membership values
clusters.technique: Complement=1-mu; intersection=min; union=max; algebraic sum=a+b-ab; bounded sum=min(1,a+b); bounded difference=max(0,a-b). Apply element-wise.
clusters.what_changes: Which operation (complement, intersection) and the membership numbers; match-the-following form in 2025.
clusters.skip_note: The 2025 match list covers every operator these compute.

clusters.title: Alpha-cut properties
clusters.technique: Alpha-cut = elements with mu>=alpha. Higher alpha gives smaller set (nested, decreasing). Union/intersection commute with cuts; complement does not except special cases.
clusters.what_changes: Nesting direction question vs. which property is invalid.
clusters.skip_note: Both reduce to 'higher alpha means smaller set'.

clusters.title: Minimax root value of a game tree
clusters.technique: Evaluate bottom-up: MAX nodes take max of children, MIN nodes take min. Alpha-beta gives the same root value.
clusters.what_changes: Tree shape, leaf values; june2019_q91 and dec2019_q60 are the same tree (values 7 vs 17 style).
clusters.skip_note: Same bottom-up procedure; the rep covers it. (Figures in q91/q60 are partly blank in the source.)

clusters.title: Alpha-beta pruning true/false statements
clusters.technique: Facts: minimax is depth-first; alpha-beta returns the same value as minimax; pruning efficiency depends on move ordering; alpha init -inf, beta +inf; values updated along the search path; best case halves depth (O(b^(d/2))).
clusters.what_changes: Which statements are listed as true/false.
clusters.skip_note: All draw on the same handful of facts listed in formulas.

clusters.title: Count models of a propositional sentence
clusters.technique: Models over n symbols = 2^n assignments; count assignments making the sentence true. For an OR of literals, 2^n minus falsifying assignments.
clusters.what_changes: Sentence (B v C vs. a 4-literal disjunction).

clusters.title: English to FOL: 'a country that borders both ...'
clusters.technique: Existential quantifier pairs with conjunction (AND), never implication.
clusters.what_changes: Only the country names (India/Nepal vs India/Pakistan).
clusters.skip_note: Identical question; answer A both times.

clusters.title: Entailment definition and properties
clusters.technique: alpha entails beta (alpha |= beta) iff beta true in every model where alpha true; False entails everything; alpha |= (b and g) implies alpha |= b and alpha |= g; Horn KB works with forward/backward chaining.
clusters.skip_note: Basic definitions, covered by the rep.

clusters.title: Knowledge-base design steps order
clusters.technique: Order: choose task domain, select atoms for propositions, axiomatize the domain, ask questions about the intended interpretation.
clusters.skip_note: Same sequence both times (answer: domain, atoms, axiomatize, ask).

clusters.title: Supervised vs unsupervised vs classification algorithm identification
clusters.technique: Supervised: regression, KNN, decision tree, logistic regression, SVM, backprop. Unsupervised: clustering, PCA, Apriori, SOM. Reinforcement: reward/punish with MDP. Regression is not classification.
clusters.what_changes: Which algorithms are listed and which category is asked.
clusters.skip_note: dec2019_q81 and dec2022_shiftii_q64 are the same question.

clusters.title: Clustering algorithm steps and k-means calculation
clusters.technique: K-means: choose k, init centroids, assign to nearest, update centroids as mean, repeat. DBSCAN: eps neighbours, core points via MinPts, expand density-connected points. Compute distance (Manhattan = sum |dx|+|dy|) to a recomputed centroid.
clusters.what_changes: Sequence ordering vs one-step numeric vs correlation statement.
clusters.skip_note: Procedure-level knowledge; rep sequence plus one centroid computation.

clusters.title: Planning and STRIPS
clusters.topic: Natural Language Processing, Expert Systems & Misc AI
clusters.technique: STRIPS is action-centric: each action has precondition and effect (add/delete lists); features are primitive or derived; no conditional effects directly. Planning graph gives heuristics; relaxation drops negative effects. Classic planning definition: init, actions, goal.
clusters.what_changes: STRIPS statements vs planning components. (june2019_q93 is tagged Knowledge Representation.)

clusters.title: GA fitness and selection probability calculation
clusters.topic: Natural Language Processing, Expert Systems & Misc AI
clusters.technique: Fitness f(x); selection probability = f(x)/sum f; the parent chosen is the one with highest fitness. Convert binary string to decimal before f(x)=x^2.

clusters.title: GA step sequence
clusters.topic: Natural Language Processing, Expert Systems & Misc AI
clusters.technique: Order: initialization/evaluate fitness, selection of parents, crossover (prob pc), mutation (prob pm), repeat until termination.
clusters.what_changes: Step labels and whether evaluation comes before selection.

clusters.title: GA crossover types
clusters.topic: Natural Language Processing, Expert Systems & Misc AI
clusters.technique: One-point: swap tails after one cut; two-point: swap middle segment; uniform: binary mask per gene decides which parent gives the gene.
clusters.what_changes: Diagram vs 'mask is used in' question.

clusters.title: GA odd-one-out: operators, encodings, selection
clusters.topic: Natural Language Processing, Expert Systems & Misc AI
clusters.technique: Mutation: random resetting, scramble, inversion, swap, bit flip. Representations: binary, real, permutation (Gray also). Parent selection: roulette/fitness-proportional, tournament, rank, Boltzmann. 'Actual count' relates to selection.
clusters.what_changes: Which category is asked; distractor invented term (Difference, Combinations, Radial).

clusters.title: GA general concepts
clusters.topic: Natural Language Processing, Expert Systems & Misc AI
clusters.technique: GA mimics evolution: selection, crossover/reproduction, mutation; stochastic hill-climbing with a population. Reproduction is the costliest step.
clusters.what_changes: Which AI technique mimics evolution / GA components.

clusters.title: Agent types, architecture and environments
clusters.topic: Natural Language Processing, Expert Systems & Misc AI
clusters.technique: Simple reflex agent uses only current percept; utility-based handles happy/unhappy; learning agent improves performance; environment properties: observable, deterministic, static, semi-dynamic (environment fixed, performance score changes), uncertain = not fully observable OR not deterministic. MAS: multiple agents with diverse objectives and communication.
clusters.what_changes: Agent type, environment property, or statement set.
clusters.skip_note: The same agent vocabulary is reused.

clusters.title: NLP components and NLU vs NLG
clusters.topic: Natural Language Processing, Expert Systems & Misc AI
clusters.technique: NLU: morphological, syntactic, semantic, pragmatic analysis (no 'meaning analysis'). NLG: text planning, sentence planning, realization. Parsing: top-down, bottom-up, dependency, Earley; SMT is not a parser.

clusters.title: ANN features and layer statements
clusters.technique: ANN: machine learning algorithm, handles large data, extracts features automatically, modelled on brain; training time grows with size; can be simulated on conventional computer; can include feedback. Information flows input, hidden, output.
clusters.what_changes: Statement combos; dec2022_q64 and dec2022_shiftii_q85 are the same question.
clusters.skip_note: Statements are the same each time.

clusters.title: Backpropagation and weight update
clusters.technique: Backprop propagates error backward from output to input; gradient descent: W(t+1)=W(t)-alpha dE/dW. Training order: initialize weights, feed forward, loss, backprop, update.
clusters.what_changes: Formula vs sequence vs A/R statement.
clusters.skip_note: All based on the gradient-descent idea.

clusters.title: NN numerical computation
clusters.technique: Neuron output = f(sum w_i x_i + bias); linear transfer multiplies by constant; sigmoid 1/(1+e^-x), derivative f(1-f); perceptron update w += eta (t - y) x.
clusters.skip_note: Same weighted-sum pattern; practise rep and dec2023_q40 once.

clusters.title: Perceptron capability
clusters.technique: Single-layer perceptron solves linearly separable functions (AND, OR, NOR) but not XOR; single layer feed-forward network.

clusters.title: Unsupervised neural nets / Kohonen SOM
clusters.technique: SOM is unsupervised, competitive learning; weight update w_new=(1-eta)w_old+eta x for winner and neighbours.
clusters.what_changes: Which network is unsupervised vs update rule.

clusters.title: ANN passage questions (June 2024 re-exam)
clusters.technique: Read the passage: ANNs are inspired by the brain; input/hidden/output layers; weights adjusted to reduce error.
clusters.what_changes: Different question on the same passage.

clusters.title: Match search algorithms to properties
clusters.technique: Greedy best-first: incomplete even in finite spaces; A*: optimal if heuristic admissible; RBFS: O(bd) linear space; know the 4th option too.

clusters.title: Match search algorithms to evaluation function / space complexity
clusters.technique: Greedy: h(n); UCS/lowest-cost: g(n); A*: g+h. Space: BFS O(b^d), DFS O(bm), DLS O(bl), IDS O(bd).
clusters.what_changes: Which property is paired with which algorithm.

clusters.title: A* optimality and heuristic admissibility
clusters.technique: A* optimal with admissible h (tree) / consistent h (graph); admissible = never overestimates; consistent = triangle inequality; A* expands all nodes with f<C* and none with f>C*; max of admissible heuristics dominates.
clusters.what_changes: Which statements about A*/heuristics are true.

clusters.title: AND-OR search
clusters.technique: AND-OR search for nondeterministic environments; OR nodes are agent choices, AND nodes are environment outcomes; a solution is a subtree with a goal at each leaf (contingent plan).

examiner_mindset: Favourite format is statement-based (Statement I/II, A/B/C/D combos) and match-the-list; pure calculations are rare.
Sequence-ordering questions (GA steps, KB design steps, k-means/DBSCAN steps, NN training steps) are a recent favourite in 2022-25.
Exact repeats are common: KB design steps (2024, 2025), country-borders FOL (2018, 2021), greedy/A*/RBFS match (2020, 2023), crossovers, ANN features (2022).
Numeric items are simple and recycle structure: fitness f(x)=x^2, fuzzy complement/min, weighted sum, perceptron update with eta=0.1.
Distractors invent plausible-sounding terms ('Difference' mutation, 'Radial' selection, 'Combinations' representation, 'meaning analysis').
Search questions were heavy in 2018-20 and almost disappeared from 2023; GA, agents and neural nets took over.
Trick traps: existential with implication, alpha-cut direction (higher alpha, smaller set), semi-dynamic environment, perceptron cannot do XOR.
Cross-unit overlap: planning/STRIPS and logic overlap with KR; clustering/k-means overlap with data-mining topics.
Never asks deep derivations, proofs, Prolog code tracing, or resolution refutation steps despite taxonomy mention; game-tree figures are described only partly.

clusters.title: Table DI: totals, sums, averages and combined values
clusters.technique: Read the needed cells, convert ratio or percent to absolute numbers (M = M/(M+F) x total; expense = % x income), then sum or divide by count.
clusters.what_changes: Table (employees by college with M:F ratio / percent expenditure of six persons / enrolment by year), the cell(s) asked, and whether the answer is a total or an average.
clusters.skip_note: Same sum-or-average-of-selected-cells routine in every paper; one clean table drill covers all.

clusters.title: Table DI: percent increase or percent more/less
clusters.technique: Percent change = (new - old)/old x 100; "A is x% more than B" divides by B (the base named after "than").
clusters.what_changes: Which two quantities are compared and which is the base; decimals are rounded to given options.
clusters.skip_note: Identical base-selection trap and formula; master the base rule once.

clusters.title: Table DI: ratios, differences and condition counting
clusters.technique: Compute each needed absolute value from the table, then take ratio (reduce to lowest terms), difference, or count rows satisfying the condition.
clusters.what_changes: Entities compared, ratio vs difference vs count, and which year or item.
clusters.skip_note: All are one or two lookups plus simple arithmetic.

clusters.title: Match communication theorists with theories/concepts
clusters.technique: Memorise author-theory pairs: Gerbner-Cultivation, Festinger-Cognitive Dissonance, McCombs & Shaw-Agenda Setting, Katz-Uses & Gratification; Barthes-Myth, Bourdieu-Doxa, Gramsci-Hegemony, Baudrillard-Simulation.
clusters.what_changes: Which theorists/concepts are listed; option permutations.
clusters.skip_note: Both are 4-item matches from the same pool of media theorists; learn the table once.

clusters.title: Buddhist concept of communication
clusters.technique: Buddhist model: multi-causality, contextualised interdependence of every communicative element (contrasted with Western models that analyse elements individually).
clusters.skip_note: Same fact (multi-causality/contextualisation) tested twice in one paper.

clusters.title: Semiotics: signs, texts and Saussure
clusters.technique: Saussure: study of signs = semiology (signifier/signified); a photograph is an open text (many readings) in semiotics.
clusters.skip_note: Small semiotics vocabulary; one revision pass covers both.

clusters.title: Types and stages of communication
clusters.technique: Interpersonal stages: Phatic, Personal, Intimate. Grapevine = informal communication.
clusters.skip_note: Basic classification recall from the same paper.

clusters.title: Colonial and post-independence education commissions and policies
clusters.technique: Memorise timeline: Charles Grant, Wood Despatch 1854, Macaulay Minute 1835 (dated 1834 in some sources/question), Curzon 1904 Universities Act, Sadler (Calcutta University) 1917, University Education Commission 1948, Secondary Education Commission 1952, UGC 1956, Kothari 1964-66.
clusters.what_changes: Commission/person named, asked as who, what or chronological order.
clusters.skip_note: All draw on one standard education-history timeline.

clusters.title: NEP 2020 and NPE 1986 provisions
clusters.technique: NEP 2020: multiple entry-exit, multi/inter-disciplinary, philanthropic participation, courses in art, design, museum admin, web design; NPE 1986: open university, rural university, navodaya.
clusters.what_changes: Which policy and which provisions are listed as correct.
clusters.skip_note: Same policy-content recall; learn the key provisions list.

clusters.title: Ancient Indian education, thinkers and philosophy
clusters.technique: Panini-grammar, Jivaka-medicine, Bhaskara-astronomy, Kanada-physics (Vaisesika), Bhartrhari-grammarian tradition; Buddhist universities Nalanda, Vikramshila, Odantpuri (Takshashila is not Buddhist monastic); Buddhism holds perception as knowledge of unique particular.
clusters.what_changes: Thinker-field matching vs odd-one-out vs school of philosophy.
clusters.skip_note: One ancient-India fact sheet covers all.

clusters.title: Institutions: founders, establishment dates and plans
clusters.technique: Know founders (Milind College-Ambedkar, Rajghat Besant-Krishnamurti, Banasthali-Hiralal Shastri, Auroville-Aurobindo), university years (Bombay 1857, Delhi 1922, Utkal 1943, SNDT 1916), IIM Indore (Ninth Plan), NID states.
clusters.what_changes: Institution list; year, founder or plan period.
clusters.skip_note: Pure factual recall; rep gives the format, facts must be learned from a list.

clusters.title: Malware and security risks
clusters.technique: Ransomware (locks data for ransom), spyware (monitors), Trojan (disguised), worm/virus; phishing/pharming/hacking are risks, firewall is protection.

clusters.title: MS Office: Word and Excel features
clusters.technique: Word: spell check, thesaurus, page orientation, mail merge (slide transitions are PowerPoint). Excel: IF/COUNTIF/VLOOKUP style formulas on a sheet.

clusters.title: Operating system, hardware and device basics
clusters.technique: OS: booting loads OS, multiprogramming, device driver, defragmentation makes files contiguous; CPU processes, RAM temporary, hard disk permanent, monitor displays.

clusters.title: Networking, internet and email services
clusters.technique: OSI 7 layers top-down: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data link, Physical; MIME for email attachments; email is cloud computing; intranet shares info internally.

clusters.title: ICT applications and emerging technology
clusters.technique: AR overlays digital information on a real place; AI used in spam filters, handles uncertain data; e-commerce and video conferencing advantages.
clusters.skip_note: Common-sense benefits and definitions; options often include one extreme "always" statement.

clusters.title: Letter and number coding-decoding
clusters.technique: Write letter positions, find the rule (mirror A=Z, alternating +2/-2, next integer cube) from the examples and apply to the new word/number.
clusters.what_changes: Rule type (reverse alphabet, shifts, cube of n+1).
clusters.skip_note: Same derive-the-rule method; practise one of each type.

clusters.title: Categorical propositions: opposition, equivalence, contradiction
clusters.technique: Square of opposition: A-O and E-I contradictory; A-E contrary (not both true); I-O subcontrary; falsity of A gives O true. Obverse/conversion give equivalents.
clusters.what_changes: Which relation is asked and the proposition used.

clusters.title: Informal fallacies
clusters.technique: Division (whole to part), composition/accident, equivocation (term used in two senses), hasty generalisation: identify via the argument pattern.
clusters.what_changes: Argument text and the option list of fallacies.
clusters.skip_note: Same fallacy-spotting skill; learn 6-8 fallacy definitions.

clusters.title: Indian logic and Hetvabhasa
clusters.technique: Nyaya syllogism has 5 members, is deductive-inductive and formal-material; Savyabhicara (erratic hetu) yields opposite conclusions; Asadharana (hetu too narrow, e.g. sound is eternal because audible).
clusters.skip_note: Same Nyaya chapter with the five hetvabhasa types.

clusters.title: Definition and terms
clusters.technique: Connotation increases as denotation decreases (species before genus); operational definition applies term if specified operations yield specified result.
clusters.skip_note: Short vocabulary of the terms/definition chapter.

clusters.title: Number series
clusters.technique: Check differences, then ratios, then second differences; for odd-term find the dominant pattern.
clusters.what_changes: Additive increasing differences, multiplicative factors doubling, or odd term.
clusters.skip_note: Same method of testing difference/ratio patterns.

clusters.title: Work, time and rate problems
clusters.technique: Work = rate x time; add rates (1/6 + 1/9 + n/18 = 1); man-hour product M1 D1 H1 = M2 D2 H2.
clusters.what_changes: Workers or machines and what is unknown.

clusters.title: Money, ratio, discount and profit arithmetic
clusters.technique: Ratios from fractions via LCM; discount from marked price; mixture cost per kg = total cost / total weight, then SP = cost x (1+gain%).
clusters.what_changes: Ratio split, discount, mixture gain, or equation of equal shares.
clusters.skip_note: Standard commercial arithmetic; one worked example for each suffices.

clusters.title: Memory: types, buffer and forgetting
clusters.technique: LTM = episodic, semantic, procedural, priming; working memory episodic buffer integrates phonological loop, visuospatial sketchpad and LTM; interference causes retrieval difficulty.

clusters.title: Learning theories, styles and methods
clusters.technique: VARK = Visual, Aural, Read/write, Kinaesthetic; Bandura observational learning: attention, retention, production, motivation; cooperative learning has individual and group accountability; cognitive apprenticeship.
clusters.skip_note: Definition recall from the learning-theory chapter.

clusters.title: Educational technology and digital tools
clusters.technique: Canva-infographics; Genially/H5P/LearningApps/Educaplay for interactive content; Mentimeter/Slido/Poll Everywhere for live polls; SWAYAM Prabha DTH channels by provider.
clusters.skip_note: Application-style tool questions; learn the tool list once.

clusters.title: Assessment: norm, criterion and authentic
clusters.technique: Norm referencing compares to peers; criterion to a standard; authentic assessment for real-task projects; formative for ongoing progress.
clusters.what_changes: Choose assessment type for a scenario.

clusters.title: Qualitative research characteristics
clusters.technique: Qualitative: process, context, description, meanings and experiences; not generalisation or rigid structure.

clusters.title: Referencing styles and abbreviations
clusters.technique: APA is a Harvard variant; APA order: author, year, title, journal, volume, DOI; ante=before, cf=compare, et al=and others, passim=here and there.

clusters.title: Statistical tests, sampling and variable types
clusters.technique: Parametric: t, F, Z; nonparametric: H (Kruskal-Wallis), U; non-probability: snowball, purposive; scores with negative marking are discrete.

clusters.title: Hypothesis characteristics and value
clusters.technique: A valid scientific hypothesis is testable, predictive and falsifiable; heuristic value means it generates further research.

clusters.title: Comprehension: science and human life (2023)
clusters.technique: Skim question stems first, then locate lines; main idea is the opening and closing sentences.
clusters.skip_note: Passage specific; one drill for method.

clusters.title: Comprehension: folk traditions and public space (2024)
clusters.technique: Answer by the author claim; reject extreme options.

clusters.title: Comprehension: rise of literary prose (2025)
clusters.technique: Main idea and purpose questions are explicit in text.

clusters.title: Ozone depletion, greenhouse gases and global warming
clusters.technique: Ozone depletion raises UV, skin cancer (melanoma, carcinoma, erythema), not teratoma; N2O is laughing gas and a greenhouse gas; warming affects hydrology, ocean circulation, acidification, sea level.

clusters.title: Water, noise and toxic pollution
clusters.technique: BOD reduces DO; cholera/typhoid/dysentery are waterborne (TB is not); nephrotoxic = kidney and hepatotoxic = liver; L90 = background noise.
clusters.what_changes: Identify the correct statement or odd one out.

clusters.title: Ecology, productivity, soil and wetlands
clusters.technique: Gross secondary productivity is total biomass gain by consumers; loam, gleyed and rendzina support earthworms; Keoladeo is an artificial wetland.

examiner_mindset: Fixed blueprint: 5 questions from each of 10 sections per paper (50 total), with small drift (Logic 7/6/5, Math 3/5/4).
Statement-selection format (A,B,C,D,E - choose correct combination) dominates theory sections.
Data Interpretation is always one table with five questions; ratio, percent and average only.
Reading comprehension is always one passage with five questions, answerable from text.
Chronology (arrange events) appears in several sections: communication, education, ICT.
Matching lists recur in HE, ICT, Communication, Environment.
Indian knowledge system flavour grows: Nyaya, Buddhist communication, ancient universities.
Qualitative research traits repeated almost verbatim in 2024 and 2025.
Never asks hard calculations; maths is single-step at class 10 level.
